title: Audit Project Manager - Capital Projects
description:
LOCATION: SCS HQ (Georgia) or MPC HQ (Mississippi) (with travel to project sites as needed)

**It is expected that the successful candidate will work onsite 4 days per week at Southern Company HQ, Mississippi Power HQ, or a subsidiary HQ. It is expected that the candidate can travel to other corporate facilities, when needed.**

JOB SUMMARY:

Southern Company is seeking an intellectually curious and collaborative professional to lead and support assurance and advisory engagements across major capital projects. The role evaluates project governance, risk, controls, and performance and translates complex project information into practical insights for business unit leadership and stakeholders. The ideal candidate brings experience in project controls, project management, construction, engineering, or risk advisory and excels at building alignment across disciplines and developing trusted relationships. Success in this role requires the ability to understand the business impact of risk, exercise sound judgment, and develop actionable recommendations that support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Capital Projects Risk & Assurance Project Manager will lead and coordinate risk-based assurance and advisory engagements across a portfolio of high-value infrastructure and energy projects. The role independently evaluates project management practices associated with cost and schedule controls, change management, contract administration, compliance, and risk management. Operating in a collaborative, matrixed environment, this individual will coordinate engagement activities from planning through reporting, collaborate with team members and subject-matter experts, and facilitate productive discussions with stakeholders. The role will partner closely with the project teams responsible for executing the work, along with shared services and senior leaders, to understand business objectives, assess the significance of risks, and communicate practical insights while maintaining an independent and objective perspective. Success requires initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to influence without formal authority, clarify responsibilities, and contribute to strong team outcomes.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Build trusted, collaborative relationships with project teams, business partners, and leaders across Southern Company and its subsidiaries.

  • Plan and perform risk-based assurance and advisory engagements related to capital projects, including evaluating compliance with internal policies, procedures, and applicable external requirements.

  • Evaluate project management and project controls practices related to cost, schedule, change, contract administration, governance, and performance reporting.

  • Apply intellectual curiosity and sound judgment to identify emerging risks, investigate underlying causes, and assess potential business, financial, operational, and strategic impacts.

  • Translate complex project information and data into clear, practical insights for project stakeholders, senior management, and the Audit Committee.

  • Develop practical, risk-based recommendations informed by stakeholder perspectives that address root causes and enable management to pursue sustainable improvement.

  • Coordinate assigned engagements, priorities, and deliverables across team members and subject-matter experts, maintaining clear communication, timely completion of engagement activities, and accountability for assigned responsibilities.

  • Lead through influence by facilitating team planning, encouraging knowledge sharing, and resolving issues collaboratively.

  • Stay informed about leading practices, emerging technologies, and industry trends in project delivery, project controls, risk management, and assurance.

  • Occasionally support departmental assignments outside the primary capital-project portfolio, including special investigations, enterprise risk assessments, and other advisory work.

  • Perform work in accordance with GIAS and applicable internal audit procedures.

JOB QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE & SKILLS:

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Business, Finance, Engineering, Construction Management, or related field required.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification is preferred.

EXPERIENCE:

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in capital project delivery, project controls, project management, engineering, construction, risk advisory, or a related discipline, including experience coordinating complex workstreams or engagements. Internal audit experience is valued but not required.

  • Prior experience in the utilities, energy, or infrastructure sectors is highly preferred.

  • Understanding of the capital project lifecycle, including how projects are planned, delivered, monitored, and closed out.

  • Prior experience with project management tools such as Primavera P6 strongly preferred.

  • Experience with data analytics and visualization tools, such as Power BI, is strongly preferred.

SKILLS

  • Strong team orientation and the ability to lead through influence, build alignment, integrate diverse perspectives, support colleagues, and contribute to collective success.

  • Natural intellectual curiosity and the ability to ask thoughtful questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and pursue issues to identify their underlying cause.

  • Working knowledge of capital project delivery, project governance, project controls, risk assessment, and internal control concepts.

  • Ability to communicate complex project and risk concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Ability to identify and evaluate risk and clearly explain its potential business, financial, operational, and strategic impact.

  • Demonstrated ability to take initiative, exercise sound judgment, and coordinate work effectively while keeping team members and leaders informed.

  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, written communication, and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to adapt to changing demands, manage competing priorities, and remain effective in a fast-paced environment.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications.

title: Senior Project Coordinator
description:

You will operate in a highly governed environment and partner closely with product, UX, operations, and technology teams to translate modeling innovation into field-ready tools that bankers trust and adopt.

Job responsibilities

  • Develop and launch AI/ML models that solve complex, ambiguous business problems in Consumer Banking, with emphasis on sales effectiveness and banker enablement (e.g., lead scoring, propensity modeling, next-best-action/next-best-offer, customer prioritization, retention, and cross-sell) using techniques such as deep learning, causal inference, contextual bandits, reinforcement learning, and constrained optimization.
  • Participate in modeling engagements end-to-end, including scoping use cases with business partners, defining success metrics (incrementality, ROI, adoption), building project plans, and working with large, complex datasets to formulate testable hypotheses.
  • Translate model outputs into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical partners, and produce narratives that drive adoption (why this lead, why now, what action, expected outcome).
  • Partner with governance, risk, and controls teams to expedite fair and thorough model reviews, document model intent and limitations, monitor performance and drift, and maintain adherence to regulatory and model risk management standards.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Advanced degree (Master’s or Ph.D.) in a quantitative discipline such as Computer Science, Statistics, Machine Learning, Econometrics, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of hands-on, relevant industry experience developing and deploying AI/ML models in production, including statistical modeling and modern Machine Learning.
  • Proficient in Python with hands-on experience in ML/deep learning frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) and core libraries (NumPy, Scikit-Learn, Pandas). Strong working knowledge of notebooks and cloud-based development/compute.
  • Deep expertise in at least one of the following, with meaningful exposure to at least one other:
    • Recommendation/decisioning systems (next-best-action/offer), ranking, and constrained optimization
    • Causal inference and uplift / treatment effect modeling for targeted interventions
    • Online learning approaches (contextual bandits, multi-armed bandits, reinforcement learning)
    • Behavioral modeling and human-in-the-loop systems that drive adoption and performance
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex modeling concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders and drive decisions.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Ph.D. in a relevant discipline.
  • Experience developing advanced AI/ML models in consumer finance, fintech, retail, marketplaces, or other high-scale customer engagement environments.
  • Experience with at least one of the following:
    • Decisioning/online learning libraries (e.g., Vowpal Wabbit, RLlib, Stable Baselines) or large-scale ranking/recommendation tooling
    • Causal inference tooling and experimentation platforms (A/B testing, CUPED, synthetic controls, causal forests, doubly robust methods)
  • Familiarity with behavioral science concepts (choice architecture, friction, habit formation) and designing interventions that are effective and compliant.
  • Experience with Databricks, Snowflake, or similar platforms; strong practical MLOps experience (model deployment patterns, monitoring, drift detection, retraining, and reproducibility).

title: Lead - Service Design
company: Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions and Transport
description:
About us

The Ministry for Cities, Environment, Regions and Transport (MCERT) takes a long-term view of how New Zealand’s towns, cities and regions grow and change. We work across housing, transport, the environment, urban development, infrastructure and investment, and partner closely with local government. MCERT is leading the implementation of the Planning System Transformation Programme. We are seeking an experienced Service Designer to join our programme and lead complex, large-scale change planning and delivery across multiple internal and external stakeholders

About the role

Reporting into the People Readiness and Change Team , you will be part of the Programme Design Function working alongside other designers and working across policy, digital, data, implementation, change, communications and other specialist teams. This is a hands-on role working alongside priority initiatives. You will help teams understand user needs, bring research and evidence into decisions, make sense of complex information, test assumptions, and connect work across the system. This role is a fixed term / secondment to 30 June 2028.

Your focus will be on helping initiatives apply user-centred practice from early planning through to implementation, while building a coherent understanding of how decisions, services and experiences connect across the wider system.

You will be comfortable working with complexity and ambiguity, using research, analysis, facilitation and design methods to help people make better decisions about how the future planning system will work in practice.

Depending on the need, you might synthesise existing research, plan targeted user research, map an end-to-end journey, create blueprints, facilitate a cross-functional workshop, develop prototypes, or test whether a proposed approach can be understood and used.

You will also work both independently and collaboratively, taking ownership of key pieces of work from start to finish while contributing to shared design challenges across the programme.

What you will do

You will:

  • Work with priority initiatives to frame problems, understand users and connect decisions across the end-to-end experience.

  • Bring together user research, readiness findings, implementation learning and system evidence, and turn it into practical implications for decisions.

  • Plan and deliver proportionate research, participatory design, prototyping and testing with relevant users and stakeholders.

  • Create user journeys, blueprints, scenarios and visual artefacts that bring complex information and future-state concepts to life.

  • Help teams understand connections, dependencies and impacts across initiatives, workstreams and the wider system.

  • Identify assumptions, evidence gaps, implementation risks and potential unintended consequences early enough for teams to act on them.

  • Facilitate collaborative problem-solving across disciplines and help teams translate insight into action

  • Lead and deliver defined pieces of work, taking accountability for the quality, usefulness and effectiveness of outputs.

  • Coach initiative teams and develop reusable methods and examples that strengthen user-centred practice across the programme.

  • Bring te ao Māori perspectives and Te Tiriti o Waitangi considerations into the approach, evidence, participation and outputs.

What you will bring:

We are looking for someone who combines strong service design capability with the ability to work collaboratively in a complex transformation programme.

You will ideally have:

  • Significant experience delivering service design, user experience or human-centred design work in complex settings.

  • Practical experience in user research, evidence synthesis, journey mapping, service modelling, prototyping and testing.

  • The ability to make complex systems, information and relationships clear, visual and usable for different audiences.

  • Strong facilitation, relationship management and influencing skills, with confidence working across multidisciplinary teams.

  • Strong sense-making and systems thinking capability, including the ability to identify patterns, dependencies, risks and opportunities across complex environments.

  • The judgement to choose methods that are proportionate to the problem, risk and decision.

  • Excellent written, verbal and visual communication skills.

  • Knowledge or understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and te ao Māori, and a commitment to growing your cultural capability.

Why join us?

This role offers the opportunity to contribute to one of the most significant reform programmes currently underway. You will work alongside experienced programme, change and transformation professionals and play a key role in shaping workforce outcomes that will support long-term system change.

Salary range

Salary range for this role is $121,414to $147,455 pa . Appointment within this range will be based on skills and experience.

Apply now

Apply directly by completing the online application form and submit your CV and cover letter. Note: your cover letter will be a key part of our assessment process, so please highlight how your experience relates to the key skills required for this role.

Location: Wellington, other major centres considered for the right candidate.

Applications close: Sunday 18th October 2026

title: Scrum Master
company: Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission
description:
Salary: Salary + 15.4% Super

About the Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission

The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission is the national regulator of Australian Government-funded aged care services.

We protect and enhance the safety, health, wellbeing, and quality of life of people receiving aged care. This includes managing complaints and feedback about the care older people receive.

We help build confidence and trust in aged care, by promoting best practice and a culture of safety and quality in the sector. We register providers and hold them to account if they don’t meet expected standards of care.

We work with providers, workers, older people, their families, and supporters to make sure they understand and uphold older people’s rights.

Meet some of our people and learn more about the Commission and our Regulatory Strategy on our website www.agedcarequality.gov.au

About the Team

The Digital Delivery Team is responsible for delivering digital products and services that support the Commission's strategic priorities and operational objectives. The team applies contemporary Agile delivery practices to ensure solutions are delivered efficiently, meet stakeholder needs, and provide value to the organisation.

The team works closely with business stakeholders, product owners, technical specialists, and governance groups to drive successful digital outcomes through collaboration, continuous improvement, and delivery excellence.

About the Role

The Scrum Master facilitates and supports Agile delivery practices across digital initiatives within the Commission. The role is responsible for promoting Scrum principles, enabling high-performing and self-managing teams, removing delivery impediments, and ensuring Agile practices are consistently applied.

The Scrum Master works closely with Product Owners, delivery teams, and stakeholders to improve team effectiveness, foster a culture of continuous improvement, and support the successful delivery of high-quality digital products and services aligned with the Commission's strategic objectives.

Position Duties

  • Facilitate Scrum ceremonies including daily stand-ups, sprint planning, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Identify, manage, and remove impediments impacting team performance and delivery outcomes.
  • Monitor team performance and facilitate continuous improvement initiatives through regular retrospective activities.
  • Collaborate with business and technical stakeholders to ensure transparency of delivery progress and risks
  • Contribute to delivery governance activities and the preparation of reporting for leadership stakeholders

Position Eligibility Requirements (Selection Criteria)

To be successful in this role you will need to demonstrate the following:

  • Demonstrated knowledge of Agile delivery principles, Scrum framework, and contemporary delivery practices.
  • Proven ability to facilitate Agile ceremonies and team workshops to achieve delivery outcomes.
  • Strong coaching and mentoring skills with the ability to build Agile maturity across teams.
  • Ability to identify delivery risks, resolve impediments, and facilitate conflict resolution effectively.
  • Builds strong and collaborative relationships with stakeholders across business and technology areas
  • Communicates complex delivery concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Applies servant leadership principles to empower teams and drive high performance
  • Demonstrates adaptability and responsiveness in dynamic and evolving delivery environments.
  • Strong organisational and problem-solving skills with a focus on achieving business outcomes
  • Commitment to fostering a culture of continuous improvement, learning, and innovation

Position Notes

  • Salary offered will be between $99,784 - $112,571 per annum depending on skills and experience. In addition, 15.4% superannuation will be paid.
  • Only candidates who hold Australian citizenship can apply. Appointment is conditional on successfully completing a national police check. For more information, please visit
  • Non-ongoing opportunity will be offered for an irregular/intermittent term. Opportunities will be offered for varying periods up to 12 months with the option to extend to a total of 24 months.
  • Merit Pool established through this selection process may be used to fill this or future ongoing or non-ongoing vacancies.

In your application, please provide a statement of claims against the position eligibility requirements (selection criteria) in no more than 600 words, including what strengths you would bring to the role, and a copy of your CV.

  • Please complete the application and submit by 19 October 2026 at 11:30pm
  • Follow our guidelines for candidate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) throughout the recruitment process.

Please contact our recruitment team on (02) 9633 3262 or recruitment@agedcarequality.gov.au for assistance with accessing our website or with lodging your application.

Specific questions about the roles can be directed to Raj Kamal by emailing Raj.Kamal1@agedcarequality.gov.au with Position title in the subject line.

title: Fire Sprinkler Apprentice

Other Qualifications:

PHYSICAL & WORK ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform Essential Job Duties.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to bend, ascend and descend step stools, ladders and stairs, kneel, lift <75lbs, reach above and below shoulders, stand and walk for extended periods of time. Employee is required to see in color, close and far distances, peripheral, depth, and adjust focus. Employee will occasional be required to balance, crouch, drive, kneel, lift <75lbs, sit, stoop, twist, and work at heights.

Work Environment:

Frequent local travel and occasional regional and non-regional travel is required. Employee will frequently be required to work inside and outside in hot/cold temperatures and be exposed to loud noises, cramped quarters, dust, fumes and odors, standing on hard surfaces, and electrical hazards frequently. Employees will occasionally be exposed to chemicals, moving machinery, uneven and slippery surfaces. Employee must consistently wear all appropriate personal protective equipment, as required by company safety policies.

Job Summary:The Mammography Assistant provides administrative, patient-care support, and technical assistance to the Mammography Department. This position serves as an important support role for mammography technologists, helping to maintain efficient patient flow, provide a positive patient experience, and ensure that the department operates in an organized and timely manner. The position combines traditional medical secretary responsibilities with patient care and technologist-assistant duties. The individual will assist with patient preparation, room turnover, stocking and maintaining supplies, obtaining outside imaging, coordinating patient appointments, and supporting the technologists throughout the patient's visit. The Mammography Assistant works closely with mammography technologists, radiologists, scheduling, registration, and physician offices to coordinate screening and diagnostic breast imaging services.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions

  • Coordinates the scheduling of mammography exams so that all exams are scheduled correctly.
  • Greets and assists mammography patients in a professional, compassionate, and timely manner while maintaining patient privacy and confidentiality.
  • Prepares patients for mammography examinations by providing gowns, assisting patients with changing, and ensuring they are appropriately prepared for their scheduled study.
  • Assists mammography technologists as needed with patient flow, room preparation, positioning support, and other non-clinical duties to promote an efficient workflow.
  • Schedules mammography appointments accurately, verifies patient information, and coordinates examinations according to physician orders and department protocols.
  • Makes patient reminder calls to confirm upcoming mammography appointments and provides patients with necessary appointment information and instructions.
  • Assists offices with urgent add-on mammography studies by coordinating scheduling, communicating with the appropriate staff, and helping ensure timely patient access.
  • Works closely with radiologists as needed to support daily workflow, obtain necessary information, and facilitate completion of mammography studies.
  • Uploads outside mammography and breast imaging studies and ensures images are available in the appropriate imaging system for radiologist review
  • Pulls and prepares prior studies one day in advance through SecureView so that all relevant imaging is available for the radiologist to review and compare.
  • Prints daily patient letters and other required departmental correspondence.
  • Folds, stuffs, and prepares envelopes for mailing patient letters, reports, and other departmental correspondence.
  • Processes incoming and outgoing calls, messages, referrals, and medical records in a timely and professional manner.
  • Responds appropriately and immediately to patient concerns, urgent situations, and emergencies, notifying the appropriate clinical staff as needed.
  • Maintains a safe, clean, and organized mammography reception and patient-care environment for patients, visitors, and staff.
  • Ensures accurate preparation, processing, and documentation of mammography orders, referrals, records, and required screening information.
  • Communicates effectively with patients, technologists, radiologists, referring providers, and other departments to support efficient patient care and workflow.
  • Ensures compliance with hospital policies, HIPAA requirements, assists as needed with mammography regulations.
  • Maintains confidentiality and safeguards patient medical information in accordance with organizational policies and regulatory requirements.
  • Mammo secretary/assistant will assist Radiology, Nuclear Medicine, Ultrasound and CT Scan Departments as needed
  • Willing to cover Athol Hospital as requested.
  • Utilizes the hospital computer system to enter information for the release and tracking of patient’s exam releases and to obtain accurate medical record information.

  • Assures that the environment of care or services is free of objects which may contribute to the likelihood of patient falls, slips or trips. Makes readily available assistive devices for ambulation. Complies with policies and procedures relating to gait belts and similar devices.

Verifies that he or she is speaking with appropriate level of loudness so that the patient hears instructions, questions, and conversations with caregiver, but that offense is not given to the patient as the result of the voice being excessively loud. Is able to differentiate problems with hearing versus problems with comprehension.

title: Head of Security & Infrastructure
description:
Head of Security & Infrastructure

Location: Remote - United States only (must reside in the U.S.)

Team: Security & Infrastructure

Reports to: CTO (you'll work directly with the CTO)

About Rise

Rise is a global payments and payroll platform built for the way modern teams actually work - across borders, currencies, and rails. We make it possible for companies to pay full-time employees, contractors, and freelancers anywhere in the world, in either fiat or digital assets, with the compliance, tax, and identity infrastructure handled underneath.

Our stack runs on Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Run, BigQuery, Google SecOps), with MySQL, a Node.js / TypeScript application layer, and Cloudflare (including Cloudflare Pages) at the edge. Settlement for stablecoin payments runs on Ethereum and EVM-compatible networks through our own smart contracts and treasury wallets. Because we move money for real people, security and correctness are first-order concerns in everything we ship.

Our Culture

We're a lean, high-trust, high-ownership team. Because we move real money for real people, we hold a high bar for correctness, security, and accountability - the work is meaningful precisely because the stakes are real. We value:

  • Ownership over hand-offs. You'll own security and infrastructure end to end and have the autonomy that comes with that.

  • Security as a default, not a phase. Handling funds and personal data means security thinking is part of every decision, not a box checked at the end.

  • Directness and low ego. We give and receive candid feedback, write things down, and prefer clarity over politics.

  • AI-first in how work gets done. We use AI agents and assistants as a core part of daily work - writing and reviewing code and Terraform, triaging alerts, investigating logs, drafting runbooks and policies, and automating the toil that would otherwise eat the day. We expect everyone to work this way and to keep getting better at it.

  • Remote-first discipline. We're a globally distributed team spread across time zones around the world, and we communicate asynchronously with a bias toward documentation and reproducibility.

What You'll Do

Working directly with the CTO, you'll own security across Rise's cloud, edge, and on-chain surfaces, and the infrastructure operations that keep production healthy. You are the first dedicated security role at Rise, but you are not starting from zero: you inherit a working program - SOC 2 certification, Google SecOps, Terraform-managed GCP, Cloudflare at the edge, and established on-chain treasury controls - and your job is to own it, harden it, and take it further. Security is the center of gravity for the role, with infrastructure and reliability close behind, on a mostly serverless stack designed to keep operational overhead low.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will not manage people, but you are the security leader for the company: you set security direction, make the calls on risk, represent Rise to auditors, partners, and customers, and are the person engineering and leadership turn to when a security or infrastructure question needs an answer. It is a builder's seat, not an advisory one - you'll harden what exists, design what's missing, and ship it yourself.

Security operations (SecOps)

  • Own and run Rise's security operations: detection engineering, alert triage, investigation, and response across GCP, Cloudflare, GitHub, and Google Workspace.

  • Build and tune detections in Google SecOps (Chronicle) over Cloud Audit Logs, load-balancer and Cloud Run request logs, Cloudflare firewall logs, and application telemetry - covering anomalous traffic, abuse, credential misuse, insider risk, and scanning - and keep log ingestion and feed health reliable.

  • Establish and track behavioral baselines so new or escalated activity stands out from normal operations.

  • Own incident response: detection, containment, forensics, remediation, and blameless post-mortems - and build the tooling and runbooks so we respond faster next time.

  • Run tabletop exercises and game days so our response is proven, not assumed.

  • Build AI-driven security automation: agent-based log review, alert triage and enrichment, and scheduled investigation passes over GCP, Cloudflare, and GitHub activity, so a team of one can cover what used to take a SOC shift.

Security posture & architecture

  • Own Rise's security posture across cloud, edge, data, and on-chain surfaces.

  • Design and enforce a zero trust access model: identity-aware access to production and internal tools, device and context-based policy, no implicit trust based on network location.

  • Own secrets management and access governance: least-privilege IAM, separation of duties, network segmentation, and audit logging as enforced defaults across production systems.

  • Harden the GCP footprint (SecOps, Security Command Center, Cloud Run, IAM, VPC, BigQuery, Secret Manager) and Cloudflare edge configuration (WAF, DNS, rate limiting, bot management).

  • Protect sensitive customer, payroll, and identity data - classification, encryption, retention, and access controls.

Blockchain & treasury security

  • Own the security of Rise's Ethereum and EVM treasury layer: treasury and ramp wallets, multisig (Safe) owners and thresholds, admin roles on our access-control contracts, and signer and key custody. Smart contract development, auditing, and on-chain monitoring are owned by the blockchain team; you partner with them on controls and custody.

  • Secure the relayer and off-chain services that submit transactions, including key management and transaction signing controls.

Governance, risk & compliance

  • Own Rise's compliance program: maintain our SOC 2 certification and lead the path to ISO 27001 and PCI DSS - control ownership, evidence collection, gap assessment, and audit coordination - and represent security to auditors, partners, and customers.

  • Own security policy, vendor and third-party risk review, and access review cycles.

  • Run security awareness and secure-development enablement for the engineering team.

  • Own data privacy risk - data residency, subject-access and deletion requests, and GDPR / CCPA obligations across the platform.

Infrastructure operations & platform reliability

  • Own the infrastructure operations behind code releases: run and improve the deployment pipelines that ship our fleet of Cloud Run services to production, and be accountable for safe, repeatable releases (rollouts, rollbacks, and release hygiene).

  • Provide day-to-day operational support for our production infrastructure - keeping services healthy and available, responding to operational issues, and doing the maintenance, upgrades, and toil-reduction that keep the platform running.

  • Build and maintain CI/CD and Terraform-managed infrastructure on GCP, with security controls built into the pipeline rather than bolted on.

  • Improve observability - logging, metrics, tracing, and alerting - so we find problems before customers do.

  • Be accountable for reliability - capacity, backups, and on-call - for systems that move money, on a mostly serverless architecture designed to keep operational load and toil low.

  • Operate and continuously improve our disaster recovery capability. Own our RTO/RPO targets, manage database backup and point-in-time recovery for our managed MySQL databases, maintain and refine failover procedures and DR runbooks, and run regular restore drills and game days so recovery stays proven, not assumed.

  • Keep the infrastructure upgraded over time.

What We're Looking For

Required

  • Work authorization. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and reside in the U.S. The company will not sponsor applicants for work visas for this position.

  • Background check. Must pass a comprehensive 7-to-10 year background check, including criminal, credit, and employment verification.

  • Experience. 10+ years in security engineering and infrastructure, including at least 3 years owning a security program or function end to end, with the judgment to set direction as Rise's first dedicated security leader.

  • Google Cloud Platform. Substantial, hands-on GCP experience - IAM, VPC and networking, Cloud Audit Logs and monitoring, Security Command Center, Secret Manager, Cloud Run, BigQuery, and Google SecOps (Chronicle). This is a GCP role; you should already operate GCP in production.

  • Security operations and incident response. You've built and run detection, triage, and response as a day-to-day discipline in a SIEM (Google SecOps / Chronicle preferred), you can turn logs into signal and signal into alerts people act on, and you've been in the room when something was on fire and helped put it out.

  • Terraform. You manage cloud infrastructure as code in Terraform and are comfortable owning the modules, state, and pipelines that apply it.

  • Zero trust. You have designed and implemented zero trust access (identity-aware proxies, Cloudflare Access / BeyondCorp-style controls, device posture, context-aware policy) for production and internal systems.

  • Security fundamentals. IAM and least privilege, secrets/key management, network security, cryptography basics, and data protection.

  • Code literacy. Comfort reading and reasoning about code in a Node.js / TypeScript and MySQL environment (you don't need to be a full-time developer).

  • CI/CD. Hands-on experience owning deployment pipelines and embedding security controls into how we build and ship.

  • Production operations. Willingness to carry production operations and on-call for a small set of VMs and a mostly serverless GCP footprint alongside the security work.

  • AI-first workflow. You already use AI tools (Claude Code, Copilot, or similar) every day to write and review code, investigate incidents, draft documentation, and automate repetitive work - and you can show how it has multiplied your output. This is how work gets done at Rise; it is not optional.

  • Compliance. You have carried at least one of SOC 2, ISO 27001, or PCI DSS through certification and recurring audits as the control owner, and know what evidence collection actually costs. Experience taking a company from SOC 2 to ISO 27001 or PCI DSS is a strong plus.

Preferred

  • Google Cloud certifications. Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer, plus any of Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Cloud Network Engineer, or Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer.

  • Ethereum / EVM security. Wallets, keys, and signers; multisig (Safe) administration; and the threat landscape around stablecoin settlement.

  • Regulated industry. Experience in fintech, payments, or another regulated, funds-handling environment.

Nice to have

  • Security clearance. Active or previous U.S. Government security clearance.

  • Military service. U.S. military experience, particularly in cybersecurity, signals, or intelligence roles.

  • Additional certifications. CISSP, GCIH, GCFA, GCDA, CCSP, or similar.

  • Cloudflare depth. WAF rules, Workers, Zero Trust, and Logpush beyond the basics.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $230,000-$275,000, commensurate with experience.

  • Meaningful equity in a growing company.

  • Generous healthcare benefits - medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family.

  • Unlimited PTO and a flexible work schedule - we care about outcomes, not hours.

  • 401(k) with a 3% company grant - not a match. Rise contributes 3% of your salary to your 401(k) every pay period whether or not you contribute a dollar yourself. Add your own contributions on top and you keep both.

  • Fully remote within the United States.

Why Rise

You'll be the person who owns security operations and reliability for a platform that moves real money across borders and on-chain. It's a role with genuine scope, genuine autonomy, and genuine stakes - GCP security, SecOps, blockchain treasury security, compliance, and production ownership, all in one seat, with a direct line to the CTO.

You'll be the first dedicated security leader at Rise, inheriting a real program and the full authority to shape where it goes next.

Job Description

Department

Activities

Reports to

Activities Director, Executive Director / Administrator

Reporting to this position

None

Job Classification

Department Staff

Position Purpose

Assists in planning, organizing, implementing, and evaluating all recreational, social, intellectual, emotional and spiritual programs, in accordance with facility policy, the resident’s care plan, and as directed by supervisors.

Required Qualifications

The Activities Aide must possess:

  1. Current/ Active Food Handlers Permit
  2. Must be at least sixteen (16) years or older
  3. Therapeutic Recreation Technician (TRT) is required
  4. Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Major Duties and Responsibilities

The Activities Aide will assist the Activities Director in creating a monthly calendar of activities written in large print and posted in a prominent location that is visible to residents and visitors.

The Activities Aide will ensure that a copy of the monthly calendar of activities in placed in a prominent spot in each resident’s room.

The Activities Aide will interview residents or family members to obtain activity preferences.

The Activities Aide will coordinate and assist residents in getting to activity locations within the facility.

The Activities Aide will assist in conducting scheduled activities to promote the physical, social, and mental well-being of residents.

The Activities Aide will document resident activity program attendance and ensure that all charted activity progress notes are informative, descriptive of the services provided, and indicate the resident’s response to the service.

The Activities Aide will observe resident mood, behavior, and degree of involvement in facility activities and report any changes or concerns to the Activities Director.

The Activities Aide will involve residents and families in planning activities program when possible.

The Activities Aide will assist with conducting in room activities programs for those residents who benefit from one on one visits.

The Activities Aide will coordinate and arrange for offsite field trips and transportation needs when necessary.

The Activities Aide will coordinate activities needs and requests with other departments in a courteous and timely manner to assure that daily activities can be performed without interruption.

  1. Treats all residents with dignity and respect. Promotes and protects all residents’ rights.

  • Attends Care Plan meetings as requested.

  3. Resourcefulness.

  5. Positive attitude.
  6. Ability to be organized and efficient.

  9. Ability to read, write, speak and understand the English language.

title: Sr. BI Data Engineer
description:
Overview

Otter Products is hiring for a Sr. BI Data Engineer to join our team in Fort Collins, CO. This position can work a hybrid schedule.

The Sr. BI Data Engineer will be the foremost expert in Microsoft PowerBI and Fabric solutions to power enterprise data initiatives, following industry-standard practices and tools. This role carries dual priorities: designing and managing high-quality semantic models and delivering compelling, trusted data visualizations that drive decision-making across the enterprise.

The Sr. Data Engineer must guarantee compliance with data governance and data security requirements while creating, improving, and operationalizing integrated and semantic models and the visualization layers built on top of them. This includes ensuring that reports and dashboards meet enterprise standards for accuracy, performance, and accessibility — enabling faster data access, consistent metric definitions, and vastly improved time-to-solution for data and analytics initiatives.

Additionally, the Sr. Data Engineer will collaborate with data architects, data analysts, and other consumers to optimize models and algorithms for data quality, security, and governance, and put them into production. This collaboration extends to co-developing visualization solutions — including semantic models, self-service reporting frameworks, and executive-facing dashboards — that surface the outputs of those models in ways that drive meaningful business outcomes and potentially large productivity gains across the enterprise.

About Otter Products

At Otter Products, we protect what’s important. From our founder’s garage in 1998 to the global technology leader we are today, Otter Products continues to drive growth through innovation and sense of purpose. Through our industry-leading brands – OtterBox and OtterCares – we provide our partners and customers the number one selling and most trusted products in our categories. Our commitment to excellence and our philanthropic spirit is the foundation on which we foster our partner relationships, allowing us to grow and to give - together. By way of our charitable arm, the OtterCares Foundation, we support our communities and invest in the future through education that inspires kids to change the world. Our founder’s core values are still at the heart of everything we do. We measure our success not just by business results, but by our ability to give back to our communities and strengthen opportunities for all. To learn more, visit https://www.otterbox.com/pages/careers

  • Act as internal expert and go-to resource for Power BI questions, conducting training and lunch-and-learns for the broader organization
  • Serve as the primary lead working with data architects to define the development of data systems, creating semantic models and optimizing ETL processes for ingest of data internally and externally
  • Act as the primary resource to collaborate with a cross-functional team to determine requirements for data needs and requirements
  • Provide technical guidance and coaching to members of the data team
  • Set the standards on Power BI Dashboard/Reporting creation

  • Design and implement a layered security model using RLS, OLS, and workspace roles for human and AI agent access to certified semantic models
  • Evaluate and recommend emerging technologies for data management, storage, and analytics
  • Support and maintain a positive safety culture by following all safety policies and procedures and actively contributing to a safe working environment
  • Other duties as required

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required. Degree in Computer Science or Mathematics preferred. Experience in lieu of degree may be considered.

title: Børne- og ungekonsulent til Lær for Livet i Aarhus
description:
Vil du være med til at styrke den sociale mobilitet for børn og unge, der vokser op i svære livsvilkår? Har du erfaring med at arbejde med børn og unge og deres familie? Og vil du være med til at skabe stærke relationer og understøtte børne- og ungedeltagelse i Lær for Livets indsatser? Så er du måske Lær for Livets nye børne- og ungekonsulent.

Lær for Livets vision er, at alle børn og unge i udsathed skal have en ungdomsuddannelse. Det er et komplekst problem, som vi arbejder for at ændre i tæt samarbejde med kommuner og fonde i hele landet. Det gør vi ved at styrke læring, livsduelighed og fællesskaber til gavn for målgruppen.

Vi søger lige nu en børne- og ungekonsulent til at understøtte børn og unges deltagelse i Lær for Livets aktiviteter til vores nye kontor i Aarhus.

Som børne- og ungekonsulent vil dine opgaver blandt andet være, at:

  • Understøtte børn og unges deltagelse gennem samtaler med børn, unge og deres voksne.
  • Matche børn, unge og mentor og opstart af mentorrelationer.
  • Deltage i og holde oplæg på velkomstarrangementer for nye børn og deres voksne.
  • Deltage på Lær for Livets camps.
  • Uddanne og understøtte Lær for Livets frivillige.
  • Opfølgning med samarbejdspartnere og kommuner.
  • Tværgående samarbejde med øvrige teams og stabe i Lær for Livet.

Om dig

  • Du trives med at arbejde selvstændigt og kan se dig selv være med til at opbygge vores nye lokation i Aarhus
  • Du brænder for at gøre en forskel for børn og unge i udsathed
  • Du har erfaring med at arbejde med børn og unge
  • Du har en akademisk profil – evt. lærer, pædagog eller socialrådgiver suppleret med en master- eller kandidatuddannelse
  • Du har erfaring med frivillighed, enten professionelt eller som frivillig
  • Du trives i en vekselvirkning mellem direkte kontakt med Lær for Livets mange børn, unge, frivillige og samarbejdspartnere og mere indadvendte opgaver som fx dokumentation og evaluering
  • Du er indforstået med, at stillingen indebærer aften- og weekendarbejde.

Om stillingen
Stillingen er fuldtid på vores nyåbnede kontor i Aarhus C. Du bliver en del af et team på i alt fem konsulenter, der sammen varetager den primære kontakt omkring børn og unge i Lær for Livet. Dine fire kollegaer har arbejdsplads på vores sekretariat i København, hvorfor der vil være en del onlinemøder og en forventning om at du tager turen til København ca. 2 gange om måneden.

I forbindelse med opstart, skal du forvente at deltage i flere møder på kontoret i København.

Du vil referere til teamleder Mira Milling. Stillingen ønskes besat pr. 1. januar 2027.

Ansøgning og kontakt
Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte teamleder Mira Milling på mm@laerforlivet.dk eller telefon 51342858 på mandage ml. kl.15-16 og fredage ml. kl. 9-10.

Send din ansøgning og dit cv via nedenstående link senest den 4.11.2026 kl. 12.00. Der afholdes ansættelsessamtaler torsdag d.12.11.2026 (og evt. 2. samtaler 18.11.2026).

Om Lær for Livet
Lær for Livets vision er, at alle børn og unge i udsathed kan gennemføre en ungdomsuddannelse. Vores mission er at styrke deres læring, livsduelighed og fællesskaber, så de står stærkere i skolen og i livet. Det gør vi gennem støtte fra frivillige mentorer, rummelige læringsfælleskaber i klubber og læringscamps og lokale fællesskaber i tæt samarbejde med kommuner og fonde. Lær for Livet arbejder ud fra et ressourceorienteret børne- og ungesyn. Det betyder, at vi er ambitiøse på alle børns vegne og fokuserer på deres styrker, potentialer, drømme og håb. Lær for Livets arbejde har dokumenteret positiv effekt for både det enkelte menneskes skolegang, trivsel, selvtillid og fremtid og for samfundet som helhed.

Lær for Livet har kontor på Roskildevej 39, 3. tv., 2000 Frederiksberg. Derudover åbner Lær for Livet kontor i Aarhus. Det samlede sekretariat i Lær for Livet består af 40 medarbejdere, der alle arbejder for at styrke den sociale mobilitet hos børn og unge i svære livsvilkår.

title: Post-Doctoral Research Associate: Department of Chemistry - UTK
description:
The position of Postdoctoral Research Associate is open in the research group of Prof. Konstantinos Vogiatzis in the Department of Chemistry at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, in collaboration with the Y-12 National Security Complex. The researcher will perform atomistic simulations of materials for catalytic applications. All candidates must have successfully defended and submitted their dissertation before their employment date. The search starts immediately and continues until the position is filled.

The researcher will be responsible to develop, test, and deploy computational workflows for atomistic modeling of chemical processed on material surfaces related to catalytic applications and collaborate with researchers from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville and Y-12 National Security Complex. Research will involve feedback loops between theory and experiment, evaluating chemical reaction networks and catalytic mechanisms. Position may require security clearance.

  • The Vogiatzis Group focuses on the development and application of novel computational modeling methods that interface classical mechanics, quantum mechanics, and artificial intelligence.

  • The ideal postdoctoral research associate candidate will work on assigned research projects as well as on mentoring of undergraduate and graduate students.

  • The postdoctoral research associate candidate must be knowledgeable and experienced in classical simulations, quantum chemical methods, materials science, catalysis, surface chemistry, and/or artificial intelligence and machine learning.

  • Responsible for presenting and reporting research results and publishing scientific results in peer reviewed journals in a timely manner.

  • Ensure compliance with environment, safety, health and quality program requirements.

  • Maintain strong commitment to the implementation and perpetuation of values and ethics.

Required Qualifications

  • Education: Must have successfully defended and submitted dissertation by hire date, Ph.D. in chemistry, physics, materials science, chemical engineering, or closely related field.
  • Experience:

    • An excellent track record of productive and creative research demonstrated by publications in peer reviewed journals.

    • Strong verbal and writing skills.

    • The candidate must be willing to work independently and collaboratively with group members, and preferably also with experimental collaborators.

  • Knowledge, Skills, Abilities: Ability to set priorities, multi-task and adapt to ever changing needs with the proven ability to function well in a fast-paced environment.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without need now or in the future for sponsorship for employment-based visa status.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience: Research experience in atomistic modeling, AIMD, MLIPs, catalysis.
  • Knowledge, Skills, Abilities: Scientific programming

Work Location

  • Knoxville, TN,

  • On site, and will travel for work at Y-12 National Security Complex.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Anticipated hiring range: $60,000 - $65,000
  • Find more information on UT Benefits here

Application Instructions

Please complete the on-line application (https://hr.utk.edu/staff-positions) for full consideration. For best consideration, provide the following in the application file before November 1, 2026:

  • Cover letter

  • Curriculum vitae

  • Transcript

  • List of three references (with current e-mail address and phone number/s) in the application file. One reference must be your current supervisor.

A review of all applications will begin immediately.

About The Department

The University of Tennessee in Knoxville is the flagship educational institution in the State of Tennessee, and the Department of Chemistry is its oldest PhD granting Department. We offer a long-standing tradition of excellence in chemical research and education, stretching from 1947, when the department granted the University’s first PhD degree, to the present. We have people from diverse cultures providing an international business environment.

The city of Knoxville is a hidden gem with a beautiful and walkable downtown, a diverse music scene, active neighborhoods, unique restaurants, and a robust offering of outdoor and cultural activities. UTK is located within easy driving distance to Asheville, Nashville, Atlanta, and the Great Smoky Mountains; and a day’s drive to Memphis, Chicago and Washington D.C. Knoxville and the surrounding counties have a statistical area population of over 850,000 people. The Knoxville region houses many leading corporations, including Bush Brothers & Company, Discovery Inc., Tennessee Valley Authority, and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

title: Administrative Associate - Office of Research, Innovation & Economic Development  - UTK
description:
The Administrative Associate II within the Division of Research Administration Support Services (DRASS) team in the Office of Research, Innovation, & Economic Development (ORIED), at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (UTK), provides operational and financial administrative support for the work of the 80+ people within DRA, and coordinates closely with the rest of the team in support of ORIED personnel. DRASS takes a shared services approach to supporting the operational and financial needs of the division, and the team has the flexibility to refocus support to respond to current and emerging needs and priorities. This position also serves as the primary archivist for digitizing and managing SPA award information previously stored in physical folders.

Invoicing and Audit Support

• Compile and organize supporting documentation required for invoicing and audits (e.g., purchase support, travel receipts/backup, service documentation). Ensure files are complete, clearly labeled and ordered in accordance with sponsor requirements, and provided within required timelines. Maintain proficiency with various DASH modules where source documents reside.

• Electronically submit invoices and financial reports to sponsors during peak periods and/or when the primary employee is absent to ensure deadlines are met and cash flow is optimized.

• Review all incoming audit requests with the Fiscal Assurance Manager to assign tasks and deadlines necessary for effective project management.

• Create and maintain a shared inventory of all audits, award details, findings, responses, corrective action, and key personnel involved.

• Coordinate with faculty, departmental financial personnel, and the SPA team to collect all required records set forth in the audit request. Create a shared digital site to compile and organize these documents.

• Coordinate with departments to ensure corrective action responses are received timely, reviewed by the Fiscal Assurance Officers for appropriateness, and submitted to the auditor by deadline.

• Assist Fiscal Assurance Officers with planning, organizing, and performing departmental reviews to support and encourage compliance in high-risk areas such as effort certification, subrecipient monitoring, and cost transfers.

• Prepare, modify, and maintain oversight of CANVAS, monitor quizzes and initiate the awarding of certificates when all modules are completed and passed.

• Maintain an inventory of internal control questionnaires and other relevant institutional records to streamline audit responses and promote consistency.

Data Integrity and Operational Support

• Generate and maintain data validation reports which include, but are not limited to, setup validation reports, labor distribution error reports, and task end date mismatch reports. These reports must be analyzed daily/weekly to monitor data quality across key functions. Coordinate with the award set-up team to ensure account errors are corrected in a timely manner. Departments will not be able to post expenses to awards otherwise.

• Assist with daily management of multiple central e-mail accounts: spa@utk.edu, spa awards@utk.edu, sfc@utk.edu, spacompliance@utk.edu, and FMC-AR@utk.edu to ensure incoming items are routed accurately and timely.

• Update PI information in DASH utilizing the TDX ticketing system in proper format to facilitate mass updates. • Update grant administrator information in DASH utilizing the TDX ticketing system in proper format to facilitate mass updates.

• Maintain master bookkeeper data to support automated account notification process.

• Administer sponsor portals to facilitate SPA user privileges.

• Coordinate with the Communications team to update the SPA website to ensure information is current.

• Prepare training materials (e.g., slide decks, quick guides, checklists, and process documentation) and manage Q&A during training sessions, ensuring participants receive clear guidance and follow up resources.

title: Child Development Specialist
description:
Position Title: Child Development Specialist

Employment Type: Part-Time

Department: Clinical

Location: Onsite New Brunswick, NJ & Surrounding areas

Our Mission:

Make a real impact. Build real skills. Grow with us.

At Positive Development, we believe every child deserves the chance to grow, learn, and thrive and every burgeoning professional deserves meaningful work that builds real skills for the future.

We work one-on-one with autistic children, helping them build communication, social, and daily living skills through play-based, relationship-focused interactions.

  • Psychology

  • Social Work

  • Occupational Therapy

  • Speech Language Pathology

  • Education and Special Education

  • Counseling

  • Medicine and Health

  • Passionate about working with children and teens

  • Curious about human development and learning

  • Patient, empathetic, and enthusiastic

Education majors, psychology students, pre-meds, nursing students, OT/SLP hopefuls, behavior technicians, camp counselors, teacher’s assistants, childcare providers, direct support professionals, and caregivers.

  • Track progress by documenting session notes and goal outcomes

o Playing on the floor/ground for up to two-three hours per session

title: ASSOCIATE, INVESTMENT CONSULTING
description:
About the Firm:

Monticello Associates, LLC is an investment consulting firm serving foundations, endowments, and family office clients in an investment advisory capacity. The firm is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with additional offices in Cleveland, Ohio, Washington, D.C., and Boston, Massachusetts. Our firm provides clients with manager due diligence and selection, asset allocation strategy recommendations, performance reporting, and all other necessary functions required to support clients in their role as fiduciaries.

In 2025, Monticello partnered with Cresset, an award-winning*, independent multi-family office and private investment firm. This combination brings together Monticello’s deep experience in endowment and foundation consulting with Cresset’s scale, comprehensive family office services, and broad private market access. The result is a powerful combination of institutional rigor and boutique personalization, delivering customized solutions to clients while opening new and exciting career opportunities for our team.

Associate, Investment Consulting:

We are actively seeking thoughtful, self-motivated, and highly principled individuals to serve as Associate, Investment Consulting. In this role, the individuals will support both the consulting team and research team through client engagements and investment manager due diligence. This position can be based in Bethesda, MD, Cleveland, OH or Denver, CO; it is a hybrid role with the expectation of three to four days a week in the office.

This role requires direct client communication, executing client-related projects, conducting asset allocation studies and quantitative analysis, preparing responses to requests for proposal, meeting with investment managers, generating research reports, and preparing quarterly client materials. As an Associate, you will be tasked with analyzing traditional and alternative investments within the context of a client's portfolio and providing thoughtful and strategic insight based on current market environments and specific client needs.

Job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Partnering with and supporting a small team of consultants responsible for advising a wide variety of endowments, foundations, and family offices.
  • Evaluating and guiding investment strategy and planning for client portfolios, as well as helping to implement the long-term goals of the firm’s clients.
  • Working closely with the research team and serving as generalist across multiple asset classes by engaging in investment manager research and due diligence.
  • Building quantitative analyses and thoughtful reports related to relevant market activity, as well as client and manager portfolio metrics.
  • Anticipating client needs based on market environment and responding to ad hoc requests with a highly-tailored approach.
  • Quarterly preparation of client materials and presentations, as well as assistance with RFPs and onboarding materials.
  • Fostering an environment of communication, collaboration, and mutual respect for internal teams and external partners.

title: Equipment Engineer, Screen Printing
description:
T1 Energy is bringing solar manufacturing back to the U.S. by building a domestic solar supply chain. Our mission is to invigorate America with scalable, reliable, and low-cost energy. Our fully operational 5GW solar module facility in Wilmer, Texas, can manufacture more than 20,000 modules every 24 hours. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, we will have produced two solar panels that will power American homes and fuel domestic AI. We're focused on building advanced American manufacturing and we're passionate about engineering a better future filled with abundant energy.

The Role

G2 is T1 Energy’s new TOPCon solar cell fab in Rockdale, Texas. The print line puts the contacts on the cell: screen printers, dryers, and firing furnaces. It is the last step before test, and the most fragile one in the flow. We’re hiring Equipment Engineers to keep them running.

You’ll own a set of metallization tools, from install through high-volume production. The set covers screen printers, dryers, and firing furnaces across the print line. It’s a hands-on role: most of your day is at the tool, and you’ll be trusted to make the engineering calls that keep it running.

This is an on-site role at G2 in Rockdale, Texas, day shift, supporting a 24/7 fab, with an on-call rotation for critical tool-downs, and cleanroom and sub-fab work in full chemical PPE. You’ll be building a fab from the ground up: your PMs, your procedures, and your fixes become the standard, and the calls on your tools are yours to make.

What You'll Do

• Own OEE, availability, MTBF, and MTTR for your toolset.

• Be first on the tool when it goes down. Make it safe, diagnose the failed component, and restore it. When you escalate to the vendor, bring clear data.

• Close root cause on chronic failures, wafer breakage, and leaks using 8D, FMEA, and Pareto, and verify the fixes hold.

• Analyze alarm histories, maintenance records, and tool data in JMP, SQL, Python, or Excel to spot failure trends before they cause downtime.

• Own the PM schedule, refine vendor PM procedures, and set critical-spares levels, then adjust both from failure history.

• Keep interlocks, over-temperature protection, exhaust and abatement interfaces, and paste and solvent handling controls working across the print line. You’ll do this together with EHS.

• Work with Process Engineering on print alignment, wet weight, screen and stencil life, and firing profile hardware.

• Bring tools through install, SAT, and qualification into production. Write down the procedures and train the technicians who run them.

Who You Are

• A hands-on equipment engineer who would rather be at the tool than in a meeting.

• Systematic about failure: you fix the cause, not the symptom, and you check that it held.

• Decisive when a tool is down and the line is waiting.

• A straight communicator with process, production, facilities, EHS, and vendors.

• Detail-oriented about alignment, print quality, and wafer breakage at the most fragile point in the line.

Qualifications

• A bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, or Mechatronics Engineering, or an associate degree with equivalent hands-on experience.

• 3+ years of hands-on equipment engineering in semiconductor, solar, or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on repair of screen printers, belt dryers, or firing furnaces, including print heads, squeegees, screen and stencil mounting, vision alignment, belt drives, and thermal zones.

• Component-level troubleshooting from electrical schematics, pneumatic drawings, P&IDs, and PLC/HMI diagnostics.

• A track record of eliminating a chronic equipment failure, not just repairing it again.

• Safe working practice with metallization pastes and solvents, high-temperature belt furnaces, and LOTO.

• Preferred: solar cell (TOPCon, PERC, or HJT) or semiconductor fab experience.

• Preferred: greenfield tool install, SAT, and ramp experience.

The T1 Way

We move fast, expect accountability, and treat people with respect. We also have a no-jerks policy: we don't tolerate big egos, bad behavior or "that's not my job attitude". Be sharp, be honest, be human. If you can hold the line and have a sense of humor, you'll fit right in.

T1 Energy is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants and do not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristics.

title: Test and Validation Lead
description:
About 1X

We’re building humanoid robots that work in any space humans exist with the mission to create an abundance of labor. Simple, but it’s not.

To do this right, we have to solve robotics, AI, software, hardware, manufacturing and operations at the same time, at scale, in a form factor that has to be safe. If you’re inspired by this, you’ll thrive here. We’ve been at this since 2014 and we’re at the point where the hard problems are behind us and the hard work is in front of us.

NEO is our flagship - a general purpose robot designed to move, learn, and operate in the real world alongside real people. We’re not demoing it, we're shipping it. We’re excited to meet you, if this excites you.

If you’ve spent your career working on problems that matter and want to see them actually reach the world - this is that moment. We’re scaling, we’re hiring with intention, and we need people who want to build something that will genuinely change how humans spend their time safely creating abundance for all.

About the Team

The Test & Validation team builds the methods, infrastructure, and data needed to understand how NEO performs in the real world. We work across Design Engineering and Reliability Engineering to validate new designs, accelerate engineering learning, and prove that critical robot systems can perform reliably over time.

Your Charter

Lead the Test & Validation Engineering team while remaining a hands-on technical leader for the most important robot-level validation challenges. You will turn engineering objectives into robust test strategies, personally develop complete-robot tests, and establish repeatable methods for task/load characterization, durability, instrumentation, and data collection.

Key Outcomes

  • Lead and develop a high-performing Test & Validation Engineering team, setting priorities, providing technical direction, and aligning execution with program needs.

  • Deliver robust validation strategies and test methods across R&D, design exploration, design validation, and lifetime reliability programs.

  • Personally lead development of complete-robot validation tests, including task and load characterization, robot-level durability testing, instrumentation, controls, and data acquisition.

  • Establish consistent standards for test design, execution, data collection, analysis, tracking, and technical reporting across the team.

  • Ensure test results are accurate, repeatable, and actionable, giving engineering teams the data needed to make informed design and program decisions.

  • Own planning and utilization of critical test equipment and lab assets, including budgeting, procurement, capacity planning, and equipment readiness.

  • Provide engineering and company leadership with clear visibility into test execution, risks, roadblocks, results, and program readiness.

Key Competencies

  • Hands-on technical leader who can move between engineering strategy, detailed test development, and team leadership.

  • Strong depth in test and validation of complex robotic or electromechanical systems.

  • Excellent understanding of instrumentation, data acquisition, mechanical actuation, fixtures, controls, and test equipment.

  • Ability to translate ambiguous engineering questions into practical, repeatable test methods that generate useful data.

  • Strong technical judgment and ability to prioritize testing against rapidly changing engineering and program needs.

  • Effective people leader who can coach engineers, delegate technical work, and maintain a high execution bar.

  • Clear communicator who can explain complex technical results, risks, and tradeoffs to both engineers and leadership.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

  • 5+ years of experience in Test & Validation, Design Validation, Reliability Test, or a related engineering role involving complex hardware.

  • Demonstrated experience leading Test and Validation Engineers through complex projects, including technical guidance, prioritization, and cross-functional execution.

  • Experience developing and executing tests for robotic systems or complex electromechanical assemblies, including robot-level task/load characterization or durability testing.

  • Hands-on experience with test equipment and methods including data acquisition, environmental chambers, vibration systems, HALT, mechanical actuation, and motor or drive-unit dynamometers.

  • Strong experience with test planning, data collection, analysis, tracking, and technical reporting.

Preferred Skills

  • Experience leading both rapid R&D/design exploration testing and longer-duration reliability or lifetime validation programs.

  • Experience establishing standardized test processes, templates, data practices, or laboratory workflows across an engineering organization.

  • Experience developing complete-robot or system-level validation methods.

  • Experience managing test equipment budgets, procurement, capacity planning, and utilization.

  • Experience working in robotics, automotive, aerospace, consumer electronics, or other complex electromechanical hardware environments.

What does a successful 1X Team Member look like?

Team members at 1X who thrive here are builders. They move fast, own their work completely, and treat time like it’s the one thing you can’t get back - because it is. They say what they mean, finish what they start, and hold themselves to a standard before anyone has to ask. We push each other to be better, and we do it with honesty and respect.

Compensation Range

$145,000 - 177,000

Benefits

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage

  • Generous paid time off, company holidays, and parental leave

  • 401(k) plan with company match (100% on the first 3% of contributions, 50% on the next 2%)

  • Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) and Health Savings Accounts (HSA) options

  • Commuter benefits (transit and parking)

  • Short-term and long-term disability, and life insurance

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental health, financial, and personal support

  • Onsite snacks and catered lunches

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, disability, military or veteran status, justice system impact, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
