title: Director, Industrial Gas & Chemical
description:
Director, Industrial Gas & Chemical

About the Role

As a member of Anova's Executive team, the Director, Industrial Gas & Chemical carries P&L-level accountability for the Industrial Gas and Chemical business — revenue growth, financial health, strategic direction, and operational performance — delivered through close partnership with Sales, Product/Engineering, Data & AI, and Operations leadership rather than direct authority over those teams. Reporting directly to the CEO, this leader sets the product strategy, owns customer outcomes, and is accountable for revenue results across both verticals, while aligning that matrix of partners around a single, coherent vertical vision.

This is a heavily product-oriented, customer-facing executive role. The Director serves as the primary voice of the customer at the leadership table — synthesizing market intelligence, customer feedback, and competitive insight into clear product and business decisions that drive growth, operational excellence, and an industry-leading customer experience. Success depends on being an exceptional cross-functional communicator: someone equally comfortable shaping a product roadmap and driving commercial strategy, who can align sales, product, data, and operations teams around a single, clear vision for the business. Alignment is not optional — this leader is accountable for ensuring every function the vertical depends on is moving in the same direction, with clarity on priorities, metrics, and the customer outcomes that define success.

Job Duties and Responsibilities:

Market Ownership & Business Leadership

  • Serve as the accountable P&L owner for the Industrial Gas and Chemical business, responsible for revenue, growth, and customer outcomes across both segments, delivered through close partnership with Sales, Product, Data, and Operations teams.
  • Act as the internal champion for the customer, ensuring customer feedback is continuously gathered, synthesized, and reflected in product, sales, and operational decisions.
  • Define the go-to-market strategy for each vertical and partner with the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) to translate it into the sales motion across Inside Sales, Customer Success, and Business Development teams.
  • Establish and monitor key performance indicators spanning revenue growth, customer retention, product adoption, and operational throughput.
  • Partner directly with the CEO and executive team on strategic planning, capital allocation, and competitive positioning.

Product Strategy & Decision-Making

  • Own end-to-end product decisions for the Industrial Gas and Chemical verticals, from roadmap prioritization through feature definition, launch, and lifecycle management.
  • Lead a dedicated Vertical Product Manager and partner with a UI/UX and application engineering team to deliver innovative, market-driven products with speed and quality.
  • Establish a rigorous product development cadence grounded in customer research, field intelligence, and data-driven prioritization.
  • Ensure products and digital tools evolve in response to market needs, emerging technologies, and competitive shifts.
  • Drive continuous product improvement, balancing innovation with reliability and scalability.
  • Partner with the CTO on the shared hardware and software platform, co-signing the platform roadmap each quarter and providing input on platform team performance.
  • Partner with the Chief Data & AI Officer (CDAO) on AI and data capabilities serving Industrial Gas and Chemical customers — including applied AI in customer-facing products and analytics — and track the customer impact of that work.

Enterprise Sales Alignment & Customer Focus

  • Partner closely with the CRO and the broader sales organization — including Inside Sales, Customer Success, and Business Development — to keep market feedback loops active and to jointly commit to demand forecasts.
  • Champion a culture of intense customer focus, ensuring every cross-functional team prioritizes the customer experience.
  • Participate in strategic enterprise sales pursuits, providing product expertise, market credibility, and executive sponsorship on critical accounts.
  • Work with Customer Success and Operations teams to ensure seamless handoffs from sale to installation to ongoing customer success.
  • Maintain a regular cadence of face-to-face customer interactions — on-site visits, executive briefings, and joint business reviews — to stay directly connected to customer needs and challenges.
  • Represent Anova at industry trade shows, conferences, and market events, building relationships, gathering market intelligence, and elevating the Anova brand.
  • Serve as a visible, credible ambassador for Anova in the Industrial Gas and Chemical markets, reinforcing the company's focus on customers, innovation, and partnership in every external interaction.

Marketing, Training & Communications

  • Direct the vertical's training, documentation, and marketing communications function to develop compelling product messaging, sales enablement tools, and market-facing communications for Industrial Gas and Chemical audiences.
  • Oversee training content and documentation so internal teams and customers have the resources they need to get full value from Anova's products.
  • Drive marketing communication strategies that reinforce brand positioning and generate qualified pipeline.

Operations & Technical Support Leadership

  • Partner with VP Operations and regional operations leaders to set demand priorities and customer-experience standards, and to hold the operations organization accountable for delivery quality and timing.
  • Partner with the vertical's Customer Support team, holding it accountable for response speed, resolution quality, and customer satisfaction.
  • Continuously evaluate operational processes and support capabilities to identify opportunities that improve speed and service for customers.
  • Ensure operational readiness keeps pace with product evolution and market growth.

Team & Partnerships

The Director, Industrial Gas & Chemical reports to the CEO and leads a Vertical Product Manager directly, with indirect oversight of the vertical's Customer Support and Training/Marketing Communications teams. This leader also partners closely with senior leadership across Sales, Product & Platform Engineering, Data & AI, Operations, and Finance to align the business around a shared vertical strategy, and with Anova's Program Management function to keep vertical initiatives synchronized with company-wide strategic priorities.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role spans all four of Anova's company-wide performance dimensions at once: revenue growth against plan, customer and account retention, product adoption, and gross margin. That breadth reflects the scope of the job — this leader owns outcomes across the full customer and business lifecycle for the vertical, not one slice of it. No single metric can be optimized at the expense of the others — growth funded by heavy discounting, or margin protected by under-serving accounts, would show up as a problem elsewhere.

What You'll Need to Succeed

The Director, Industrial Gas & Chemical is expected to exemplify and reinforce the following in all aspects of leadership:

  • Intense Customer Focus — Every decision begins and ends with the customer. The Voice of the Customer is not a program; it is a discipline.
  • Speed & Innovation — Markets move fast. We move faster. This leader drives urgency without sacrificing quality or customer trust.
  • Ownership — This role operates with the mindset of a full P&L business owner: accountable, decisive, and committed to outcomes over activity. The Director owns every product decision and every customer outcome in the Industrial Gas and Chemical markets, and is accountable for the revenue and growth of the business — delivered by aligning closely with sales, product, data, operations, and finance partners through Anova's structured cross-functional planning and review process, rather than working in isolation.
  • Operate At Our Best — Great outcomes require alignment. This leader builds bridges across functions and ensures no team operates in isolation.
  • Market Dictates the Roadmap — Products and services are shaped by what the market needs, not internal assumptions. Customer intelligence drives strategy.

Minimum Requirements

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in business leadership, product management, or commercial roles within industrial gas, chemical, or related industrial markets.
  • Proven track record of owning a P&L or equivalent market-level business accountability with measurable revenue and growth outcomes.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams through influence in a matrixed organization.
  • Deep understanding of enterprise sales cycles and the ability to partner effectively with sales organizations at senior levels.
  • Strong product management acumen, with experience driving product roadmaps from concept through delivery.
  • Exceptional customer orientation — a track record of building Voice of Customer processes and translating customer insight into business and product decisions.
  • Outstanding communication and executive presence; able to represent the company credibly with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders at all levels.
  • Background in B2B SaaS/HaaS or technology-enabled service businesses.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience in the industrial gas, chemical, or process manufacturing industry.
  • Experience overseeing or closely partnering with engineering and product development functions.
  • Familiarity with multi-region field operations management.

Physical Requirements

  • Extended sitting during office work, travel, and meetings.
  • Standing and walking through customer sites, field locations, and trade show floors.
  • Occasional lifting up to 25 lbs. (marketing materials, samples, demo equipment).
  • Visual and auditory acuity for presentations and face-to-face interactions.
  • Ability to work in varied environments, including industrial and outdoor settings.
  • Manual dexterity for standard office and mobile technology.

Travel Requirements

  • 30–40% annual travel expectation, dictated by business need.
  • Trade show and conference attendance, including multi-day and weekend travel.
  • Valid driver's license and passport required.
  • Ability to manage a variable, demand-driven travel schedule independently.

ABOUT ANOVA

We are very proudly “one” Anova — built by integrating the best in IIoT technology and expertise. Anova monitors more than 1,250,000 assets across nearly 80 countries for over 2000 clients, from family businesses to the largest LPG, Industrial Gases, and chemicals companies in the world. Our scale is global. Our service is local. We partner directly with customers, taking a holistic approach and delivering tailored solutions that drive innovation and improvement and make our world safer, more efficient, and reliable.

We believe that rewarding work should reward you. As part of Anova, your work, integrity, and commitment are rewarded through competitive compensation and reward strategies, through sincere appreciation, and through opportunities for growth and advancement. We put people first by providing benefits that support your life and well-being, from health and finance to recognition and reward, and so much more — we've got you covered.

If this sounds like a fit for you, apply to join Anova in connecting the industrial world — for better.

For more information about how Anova is transforming the Industrial IOT industry, visit us at Anova.com.

title: Structural Engineering Intern- Summer 2027
description:

Through our Developing Professionals Network, interns gain mentorship, networking opportunities and lifelong career connections.

title: Quality Control Inspector
description:
Purpose

The Quality Control Inspector will be required to comprehend specifications to determine testing and inspection procedures and equipment to be used. The candidate must be able to read dials or digital displays, compare results with specifications, record test and inspection data, and confer with engineers, technicians, and production personnel. The candidate must demonstrate the ability to perform dimensional checks and visual verifications of raw material, fasteners, fabricated parts, and machined parts to acceptance criteria; document and track non-conformance reports and material; and work with minimal instruction and supervision.

Location

Group Functions

Essential

  • Demonstrate advanced ability to perform dimensional checks and visual verifications of fabricated and machined parts to acceptance criteria.

  • Uses measurement and test equipment, including Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM), Faro Arms, and functional gages, to determine whether products meet all stated requirements.

  • Validate the quality of machined and fabricated parts and assemblies in terms of dimensional accuracy and visual verification according to acceptance criteria.

  • Ability to review data supplied with material and parts against acceptance criteria, including dimensional reports, Material Test Reports (MTRs), traceability reports, and certificates of conformity.

  • Liaise with suppliers as required to ensure acceptable product, documentation, and service quality is maintained.

  • Understand and adhere to requirements for gage calibration and Measurement System Analysis (MSA).

  • Develop and maintain inspection plans per drawing requirements.

  • Interpret inspection results.

  • Assists more experienced technicians and professionals in technical tasks.

  • Performs technical work tasks requiring moderate technical experience.

  • Checks in with supervisors routinely, successfully completes tasks as requested, and begins to think independently about solutions for recurring equipment-handling problems.

  • Elevates issues when they are beyond the scope of the position.

  • Applies routine techniques and standards under moderate supervision.

  • Shows initiative and enthusiasm to strengthen foundational understanding of the work area, gain exposure to related work areas, and acquire new skills.

  • Works under well-defined procedures and guidelines that require low levels of troubleshooting.

  • Mentors or provides technical guidance to junior inspectors and technicians.

  • Performs a range of tasks with autonomy and may act as a cross-departmental technical lead.

  • Applies a range of techniques and standards autonomously.

  • Shall be utilized as a subject matter expert in quality control techniques.

  • Displays advanced professional communication and interpersonal skills when exchanging information with peers and supervisors.

  • Often serves as a resource to others in resolving complex problems.

  • Ensures all existing working procedures, practices, and systems are followed.

  • Ensures in-date calibrated measuring equipment is used for performing inspections.

  • Issues, documents, investigates, and tracks non-conformances and inspection records in the following SmartSolve modules: Inspection Management, Non-Conformance, and Corrective Action/Preventive Action.

  • Shall be capable of completing inspections such as FAT, SIT, FAI, In-Process, Final, and Receiving inspections.

  • Works as a team member when performing or witnessing inspection and/or testing for internal and external customers, third parties, customer inspectors, and engineering/manufacturing representatives.

  • Assists in developing and improving quality system procedures, work instructions, flow charts, and associated process improvements.

  • Uses safe material-handling and preservation techniques, including operating a forklift and jib cranes and using packing/preservation methods to prevent deterioration or damage.

  • Product identification responsibilities include verification and/or physical product marking for traceability.

  • Supports customer satisfaction and loyalty processes.

  • Supports the organization’s drive toward excellence in Health and Safety performance.

  • Support includes, but is not limited to, participating in STOP observations, reporting HSE observations, attending HSE-related meetings, supporting HSE improvement projects, and performing any other related task deemed appropriate by the Manager.

  • Supports the MDI process by backing up the Quality Control Supervisor as needed to compile metrics and lead meetings.

Non-Essential

  • Other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities.

Reporting Relationship

  • This position reports to the Quality Control Supervisor.

Qualifications

Required

  • Minimum of 7 years of experience and/or training, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Minimum of 7 years of experience with advanced measurement techniques.

  • Minimum of 7 years of experience using advanced quality inspection techniques.

  • Basic understanding of Statistical Process Control.

  • Knowledge of ISO 9001 requirements.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, and document management software, such as Kofax and Adobe.

Desired

  • Associate degree or equivalent from a two-year college or technical school.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office.

  • Knowledge of NDT methodologies.

  • Knowledge of welding methodologies.

  • Experience operating Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMM) for dimensional inspection and product verification.

  • Experience using Faro Arm portable coordinate measurement systems for dimensional inspection and verification.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Other Characteristics

  • Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

  • Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

Working Conditions

This position is considered SHOP WORK and is characterized as follows:

title: Director, Sustaining Engineering - Spark
description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About the Role:

Crusoe is a vertically integrated AI Factory company with a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. Our competitive advantage, "Speed is the only moat," is directly tied to our ability to rapidly design, manufacture, and deploy our own modular power and compute infrastructure.

We are seeking a Sustaining Engineering Leader to own how Spark performs after it is deployed. Product Management defines the next generation. New Product Introduction delivers it into production. You own each generation from the moment it leaves ramp: fleet reliability, field failures, configuration, obsolescence, and the design changes that keep deployed units performing for their full service life.

You do not set the roadmap and you do not run the factory. You own the installed base, and you are the evidence source Product Management and NPI both depend on. You will start as the single-threaded owner of this function and build the team as the fleet grows.

First Year Mandate

Spark deployments begin in early 2027. You will build the system before there is a fleet to run it on.

  • Stand up FRACAS, the root cause evidence standard, and the Failure Review Board.

  • Establish the as-built configuration baseline before there are units to reconcile.

  • Define spares, service intervals, and repair versus replace policy for the first generation.

  • Participate in the production release and ramp readiness reviews for the first deploying generation as the receiving organization.

What You'll Be Working On:

I. Fleet Ownership & Field Issues

  • Transfer of Ownership: Take technical ownership of each generation once it completes production ramp, through a defined handover from New Product Introduction covering the released configuration, open issues, and known risks.

  • Fleet Reliability: Own failure rate by subsystem, mean time between failures, and repeat failure rate, and define the telemetry every unit must report to make them measurable. Data Center Facility Operations owns uptime and time to repair.

  • Closed Loop Corrective Action: Run FRACAS and chair the Failure Review Board. Close every failure with a root cause, a verified fix, and proof it worked. A unit that fails while built within released tolerances is a design issue; attribution unresolved after ten business days proceeds as a Spark-funded fix and escalates to the Spark GM.

  • Containment: For safety or fleet-wide risk, contain first and settle attribution after. Own the retrofit decision and its sequencing.

II. Change, Configuration & Obsolescence

  • Post-Release Change Control: Own engineering change for generations in the field, with cost and fleet impact quantified before approval. New Product Introduction owns change control up to production release; you own it after.

  • Configuration Control: Own the configuration baseline and define what Operations records. Reconcile as-maintained against baseline so a change targets exactly the units that need it.

  • Obsolescence: Run a proactive DMSMS program. Model last time buys against fleet demand and qualify alternates before a shortage forces the choice.

  • Retrofit & Maintenance: Issue engineering change packages, kit definitions, preventive maintenance intervals, and acceptance criteria. Operations executes and returns the records; you verify effectiveness.

III. Feeding Product Management and NPI

  • Requirements into Product: Convert fleet evidence into quantified design requirements. Product Management decides what enters the PRD.

  • Qualification Requirements into NPI: Supply field-derived requirements and acceptance criteria, so a failure the fleet has already seen must be designed out and proven before the next generation is released.

  • Total Cost of Ownership: Own the reliability and service inputs to Spark unit economics.

  • Serviceability Advocacy: Represent serviceability and maintainability in design reviews. You hold no approval authority; you make the case with fleet data.

What You'll Bring to the Team:

Education

  • Required: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Reliability, or a closely related engineering discipline.

Experience

  • 10 to 15 years in sustaining, reliability, or product support engineering for deployed capital equipment or infrastructure hardware.

  • Direct ownership of a fielded installed base, with field data converted into design change that measurably reduced failure rate or service cost.

  • Obsolescence and lifecycle management on a product whose service life exceeds that of the components inside it.

  • Experience standing a function up from nothing, including the processes and the partner agreements behind it.

Technical Depth

  • Reliability: FRACAS, structured root cause analysis, and mean time between failures and population failure rate analysis.

  • Change & Configuration: PLM, change order workflow, as-built control, and serial level effectivity.

  • Obsolescence: DMSMS practice, end of life monitoring, last time buy modeling, and alternate part qualification.

  • Systems Fluency: Electrical, mechanical, and thermal command sufficient to adjudicate root cause on a modular power and compute product, including liquid cooling.

  • Service Economics: Spares, service cost per unit, and the link between availability and revenue.

Additional Qualifications

  • Experience with modular, containerized, or prefabricated infrastructure products in the field.

  • Familiarity with liquid cooled data center hardware, including CDU and rack level cooling interfaces.

  • Mountaineer Spirit: The persistence to chase a root cause past the easy answer, and the judgment to know when a fleet-wide fix is worth its disruption.

title: Contact Record Update Assistant
description:
Contact Record Update Assistant

Office Administration | Contact Records | Remote | Full-time
56,680–59,800 per year

People change addresses, phone numbers, and email contacts. The remote Contact Record Update Assistant handles the ordinary administrative steps that keep those details current in an online customer record. The result should be straightforward: the approved information appears in the correct record, and a change that needs more checking stays with the person authorized to review it.

Typical changes

  • Find a customer record using the identifiers supplied in a request.
  • Compare the new contact detail with the existing entry.
  • Enter approved changes in the assigned fields.
  • Check the saved record for spelling, numbers, and accidental omissions.
  • Note incomplete or conflicting requests without guessing.
  • Send a question or handoff through the established process.

A message may contain a new phone number and an email address but omit the detail needed to match the correct customer. In that situation, the important work is to leave the request pending and seek clarification using the employer’s procedure. Another message may describe two people with similar names. Read the available information before choosing a record; making a quick change to the wrong account can create more work for the customer and the team.

What stays outside your authority

Some details have a greater impact than a routine contact update. A request to change account ownership, payment instructions, or another protected field should be referred rather than treated as a normal correction. You will work within approved access and information-handling rules. The employer will teach its specific verification steps; the starting expectation is that you will stop and ask when a record cannot be matched confidently.

After a permitted change, look again at the finished record and note that the update was completed. If the same request arrives twice, check whether an earlier entry has already been made before saving another one. When a colleague receives a follow-up question, your brief status note should explain what changed and what remains unresolved.

Recordkeeping can involve more than a single field. A customer may provide a corrected mailing address but ask that an existing email contact remain unchanged. Read the full request before editing, then compare each saved field with what was authorized. If part of the request falls outside the routine process, keep that part open for review instead of treating the entire message as completed.

What the work calls for

  • Care with names, digits, and small differences between records.
  • Comfort entering information through online forms or a database.
  • Short, clear email replies when information is missing.
  • Respect for private customer details in a home office or other suitable space.
  • Willingness to follow an established process and correct mistakes promptly.

Previous data entry, customer service, or office administration experience can help, but none is required. full-time scheduling may be available; actual hours will be confirmed for the opening. Remote work requires a suitable computer setup for handling records privately.

title: CNC Programmer
description:
Job Title: CNC Programmer

Job Location: Office & Production floor

Reports to: Engineering Supervisor

Job Responsibilities:

  • Develop, optimize, and maintain CNC programs for multi-axis machining centers.
  • Determine tooling strategies, cutting parameters, and work holding solutions to maximize productivity and quality.
  • Perform program proof-outs, first article inspections, and process validation.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on cycle time reduction, setup reduction, and cost savings.
  • Collaborate with Technical Planning, Quality, and Production to resolve manufacturing issues and improve throughput.
  • Create and maintain manufacturing documentation, setup sheets, work instructions, and tooling lists.
  • Support MRB, corrective actions, and root cause investigations related to machining operations.
  • Utilize GD&T requirements to ensure manufacturability and compliance of machined components.
  • Produce solidworks models from existing aircraft drawings
  • Establish Mfg. required processes including any allowances for special processing or future assembly.

Education, Skills & Experience:

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Minimum 5 years of CNC programming and manufacturing engineering experience in a precision machining environment.
  • Proven ability to apply practical and advanced manufacturing technologies. This includes applying the principles, techniques and procedures required to design and create a manufacturing process to produce various aircraft parts and assemblies utilizing various equipment available.
  • Knowledge of raw materials, production processes, quality control, costs, and other techniques for maximizing an effective, efficient manufacturing process.
  • Experience programming 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis CNC Machining centers.
  • Strong understanding of GD&T (ASME Y14.5)
  • Ability to read and interpret aerospace drawings, specifications, and customer requirements.
  • Experience with process development, routing creation, and manufacturing planning.
  • Knowledge of aerospace materials including aluminum, stainless steel, titanium, Inconel, and specialty alloys
  • Experience selecting tooling, feeds, speeds, and machining strategies for complex components.
  • Experience with ERP/MRP systems and electronic manufacturing documentation.
  • Strong problem-solving and root cause analysis skills.
  • Experience supporting AS9100 and customer quality requirements preferred.
  • Experience with various CNC equipment (Vertical Mills, Horizontal Mills (including 5 axes), Lathes with live tooling and various manual equipment.
  • Extensive experience with SolidWorks and/ or NX for 3D modeling, design, and manufacturing support.
  • Advanced CAM programming experience using Gibbs CAM, Siemens NX, Mastercam, or equivalent software. NX preferred.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities while meeting production deadlines.
  • Capability to work within a team environment
  • Attention to details characteristics.

Physical demands

  • Position may require use of hands & arms with repetitive motion & reach.
  • Position may require manual dexterity for handling tools and equipment.
  • Work is performed while standing, sitting and/or walking.
  • Position may require the ability to communicate effectively using speech, vision, and hearing.
  • Position may require the use of hands for simple grasping and fine manipulations.
  • Position may require bending, squatting, crawling, climbing, and reaching.
  • Position may require the ability to lift, carry, push, or pull medium weights, up to 30-75 pounds (50-75 lbs. would have partner assistance)
  • Position may require activities involving being around moving machinery, exposure to marked changes in temperature and humidity, and exposure to dust, fumes, and gases.

Work Environment

The plant is a machining environment; therefore, you may be required to wear respiratory protection due to airborne particles, chemicals & solvents depending on position.

Safety glasses are always required in production areas. OSHA regulations are followed.

title: System Administrators
description:
Are you a tech-savvy professional looking to break into a new field. If so, we have a great opportunity for you!

Become a Mainframe Software System Administrator through a paid 6-month immersive training and a 6-month residency.

Applications Accepted: Oct 5, 2026 to Oct 16, 2026
Training Schedule: Feb 1, 2027 to Jun 25, 2027, Full-Time, Monday-Friday, 40 hours/week

Location: Wellington, Sydney, Melbourne.


Entry-Level Mainframe Software System Administrators

We have an immediate paid training and job opportunity for entry-level mainframe systems engineers with a Fortune 500 Company for individuals open to relocating.

Don't have experience with mainframe yet? Don’t let that discourage you! Selected candidates will participate in a 12-month paid training and residency program. The immersive, comprehensive training curriculum spans 6 months, starting at AUD $30/hour full-time, with a pay increase to AUD $34.00/hour full-time once the 6 month Residency period starts. After relocating (if required), candidates will participate in a 6-month residency, receiving on-the-job mentorship. Successful candidates will convert to permanent employment with the Residency company, accompanied by a salary increase and a AUD $7,500 completion bonus.


For many companies, their technical architecture is dependent on mainframe systems. However, most Universities no longer teach mainframe development, and many developers are retiring. Gaining mainframe experience can get you on the road to a high-paying, secure career.


How Does the Process Work?

At Facet, we know the job search is complicated. Here is an overview of what you can expect from our application process:

Phase 1 : Written Application. Start your application above by providing demographic information and responding to a series of questions.

Phase 2: Resume and Informational Questionnaire. Final applicant pool candidates will undergo rounds of resume revision until approval and complete an informational questionnaire.

Phase 3: Technical Interview with Facet. Those same selected candidates will also be required to interview virtually, live with a Facet representative. They will provide more detail on the program and include technical questions to assess technical skills.

Phase 4: Interview with Fortune 500 company, Broadcom. Candidates will participate in mandatory interview preparation sessions before interviewing with our partner company.

Phase 5: Start Training. Selected candidates will begin the 6-month training in February 2027, with potential relocation within Australia for the 6-month residency commencing August 2027.

The ideal candidate meets all of the requirements and has:

  • Experience that demonstrates technical knowledge; for example, back-end programming language and operating system; network administrator, cyber security, IT/help desk, are ideal skill sets

  • Eagerness to learn problem-solving techniques in Unix-based or Mainframe operating systems

  • Desire to work from the command line and understand the needs of users and team members

  • Curiosity about the software development life cycle, data management, security, and agile work environments

  • Passion, drive, and aptitude to succeed

Requirements for this opportunity include:

  • New Zealand and/or Australian Citizenship or Permanent Resident status

  • 3-year degree in any major

  • Willingness to relocate


FAQs

How does training work? What is the timeline?

The entirety of the 6-month paid training is remote and instructor led online from your own home. The material is designed to give you an overview of IBM Z system, knowledge of mainframe programming languages, practice with mainframes, and then product-specific training in one of different areas: Security products like ACF2 and Top Secret, Endevor, IDMS, Datacom, or OPSMVS. Skills will be delivered in a blend of remote, instructor-led (this is the majority of the training), web-based and self-paced accelerated learning path. Finally, after training, you will relocate and begin your residency with the hiring company. You will receive 1-on-1 mentorship and the ability to convert to a full-time employee.

How is working on the mainframe similar to open-source software development?

The concepts are very similar, but the programming languages you use (JCL, REXX, and Assembler) have different syntax. If you already know Java, that's great, because it is often used in the mainframe. SQL skills also translate well, as you will interact with similar databases.

What makes mainframes so important?

Mainframes have run for more than 50 years with 71% of Fortune 500 companies utilizing them. They handle over 12.6 billion credit card, ATM transaction per day. They are central to many companies' technological infrastructures, so they are crucial for many businesses.

How do I know mainframe is right for me?

Here are a few resources you can utilize to gauge your interest in mainframe. IBM Z Xplore is a free platform where you can get hands-on experience across fundamental to advanced concepts like JCL, Linux, and TSO/ISPF. 'What on Earth is Mainframe' is a good introductory book on z/OS operating systems.

How many hours per week is training?

Training is full-time, 40 hours/week, M-F.

Will I get paid during training?

Yes! You will get paid AUD $30/hour for the first 6 months of the training with a pay increase to AUD $34.00 when the 6-month Residency period starts. After the residency is completed, the hiring company has the option to convert you to full-time employee where you would receive a AUD $7,500 compensation bonus.

How likely am I to convert to full-time?

Very likely. Our partner’s Customer base works with our Partner with the full intention of hiring, so if you show up every day and work hard, your chances are very good.

Where will the final jobs be?

The final job will be determined by the location of our customer. Whilst we will try and match you with a customer in your preferred location, we cannot guarantee any city. We are looking for candidates who will relocate with an open mind.

How much money would I make after conversion?

Candidates who complete the paid training and residency with our partner company should expect a starting salary between AUD $90,000 to AUD $120,000.

Is the program available to individuals requiring Working visas?

Unfortunately, no. The program is only available to individuals who can legally work in New Zealand or Australia as Citizens or a lawful permanent resident.

title: Staff / Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Reinforcement Learning
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Engineering Teams

The Driving Core team develops the learning methods that turn diverse driving data into robust closed-loop behavior. You'll be a technical owner for reinforcement learning within the group, working closely with researchers and engineers across AV Core, Simulation, Evaluation, and Product Engineering. Success means producing measurable improvements in driving behavior.

The Core Model Safety team develops the core model competencies that enable safe, driverless operation. In this team, you'll lead the technical direction and delivery of a learned emergency trajectory model for low-frequency, high-consequence manoeuvres such as evasive steering and emergency braking, taking the programme from problem definition through modelling, evaluation, integration, and evidence for deployment.

🧠 Your day-to-day

As a Senior / Staff Machine Learning Engineer in Wayve's AV Core organisation, you will advance reinforcement learning methods for end-to-end driving models. You'll identify where learning from reward or feedback can improve beyond behavior cloning, then take promising ideas from design through large-scale experiments, rigorous evaluation, and integration into our best driving models.

🧩 What you’ll be working on

  • Shape and execute the reinforcement learning roadmap for Driving Core / Core Model Safety, selecting problems and methods against clear behavioral gaps and measurable success criteria.

  • Develop and evaluate post-behavior-cloning optimization methods, including offline and off-policy reinforcement learning as well as other reward-guided approaches; design the regularization, data strategy, and diagnostics needed to make policies reliably better.

  • Help improve the reward models and related learning signals used to train and evaluate driving policies, working with partner teams to strengthen their quality, scalability, and downstream usefulness.

  • Build robust training and experimentation workflows using large-scale driving data; diagnose distribution shift, objective misspecification, optimization instability, and data or evaluation bias.

  • Define evidence across offline metrics, open-loop tests, closed-loop simulation, and on-road evaluation, and distinguish genuine policy improvement from benchmark overfitting.

  • Productionize successful methods in the shared ML stack, communicate decisions and results clearly, and raise the technical bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentoring.

🙌 You should apply if

Essential

  • You have a strong track record developing and experimentally validating reinforcement learning or closely related sequential decision-making methods on complex, high-dimensional problems.

  • You have a deep understanding of modern reinforcement learning fundamentals, including policy and value learning, off-policy learning, function approximation, distribution shift, and the failure modes of learned objectives.

  • You have hands-on experience with behaviour cloning, reinforcement learning, or related methods.

  • You're proficient in Python and PyTorch, with strong software engineering practices and hands-on experience building reliable machine learning training and evaluation systems.

  • You have excellent experimental judgement: able to turn an ambiguous behavioral problem into falsifiable hypotheses, useful metrics, disciplined ablations, and clear technical decisions.

  • You bring senior-level ownership and collaboration: able to lead a substantial technical area, work across research and engineering boundaries, and bring others along through clear written and verbal communication.

Desirable

  • Experience with offline reinforcement learning, imitation learning, reward modeling, preference learning, or post-training of large neural policies.

  • Experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, control, or another domain where policies interact with safety-critical physical systems, including an understanding of motion planning, vehicle dynamics, control, or collision avoidance.

  • Experience with closed-loop simulation, off-policy evaluation, uncertainty or calibration, and evaluation under rare or shifted conditions.

  • Experience training multimodal, transformer-based, or generative policy models at scale.

  • Proficiency in C++, CUDA, distributed training, or performance optimization for production machine learning systems.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working:

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process:

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

  • Initial call / recruiter screen [ 30 mins]

  • Competency Interviews [hiring manager interview and applied ML interview; 2 hours total]

  • Deep-dive technical interviews [programming, systems design & PyTorch debugging / technical leadership interviews; 3 hours total]

  • Final interview: mission & values alignment [Director or VP interview; 45 minutes].

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant):

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Experience Design Senior Associate - Agentic
description:
Shape the future of employee experience by contributing to the design of agentic AI and adaptive digital experiences, empowering over 320,000+ employees to enhance their productivity and growth.

As an Experience Design Associate within the Employee Experience Design team, you will support the creation of AI-driven, adaptive user experiences that respond to user intent and evolving needs across self-service journeys. Drawing on strong expertise in experience design principles, interaction design, and research practices, you will partner closely with product, engineering, and research to deliver clear, scalable, and user-centered solutions, often working in parallel with engineering from concept through build.

Your work will focus on small to large-sized features and end-to-end journeys, with a hand in shaping a growing agentic design system and defining how systems respond across varied user inputs and scenarios. At the Senior Associate level, you are expected to work independently, lead design decisions from ambiguous problems through delivery, elevate the team's craft, and help evolve adaptive, conversational, and UI-driven interaction patterns that create consistent and intuitive employee experiences.

Job responsibilities

  • Lead the design and delivery of user experiences for small to large-sized features, features and end-to-end journeys, balancing user needs, business goals, and design standards.

  • Own response mapping for your feature areas, defining system behavior across user inputs, edge cases, failure states, and handoffs between conversational and UI-based interactions.

  • Design user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity interfaces that support intuitive and scalable self-service experiences.

  • Set and uphold a high bar for interaction and visual craft, including motion and transitions, and ensure it carries through to what ships.

  • Operate with an iterative design mindset, incorporating feedback, research insights, and usability testing to continuously improve experiences.

  • Partner with engineering throughout the build, working from shared specs and co-creating in code or prototyping tools to close the gap between design intent and implementation.

  • Contribute to the development and evolution of an agentic design system, including reusable components, patterns, and interaction models.

  • Incorporate accessibility and inclusive design best practices into all work to support a diverse range of users.

  • Utilize data, research, and user feedback to inform decisions and refine design outcomes.

  • Present and defend design decisions and rationale to team members, partners, and senior stakeholders.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • 3+ years in a user experience design or equivalent role dedicated to improving experiences with digital products and services
  • Proven ability to create visually appealing and functional designs using industry-standard tools (e.g., Figma, Sketch, or Adobe Creative Suite)
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and optimizing user experiences across multiple platforms, including web, mobile, and other digital channels
  • Previous experience interpreting complex data and transforming it into actionable insights for informed decision-making

  • Proven use of generative AI assistants and LLM-powered tools within the design process.

  • Proficient understanding of inclusive design principles, accessibility guidelines, and assistive technologies, with a history of creating accessible and inclusive digital experiences

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Expert using Figma, Figma plug-ins, and FigJam.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, including rationale and storytelling that persuades senior leaders or aligns multiple stakeholders

  • Expert in the latest AI technologies and trends including Claude, ChatGPT, and other LLMs.

  • Broad Design skillset with an adaptable, product-oriented mindset and a love for learning

  • Strong understanding of technology and/or coding experience with front-end frameworks (HTML, CSS, React), experience in mobile development (iOS, Android) and using APIs.

description:

Applicants selected will be subject to a U.S. Government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. Due to the nature of work performed within our facilities, U.S. citizenship is required.

Responsibilities for this Position

Job Description:

Responsibilities for this Position

The Portfolio Risk Program Manager reports to the Segment Director and provides portfolio-level leadership for risk and opportunity management while directly managing assigned small, discrete programs. The role strengthens execution rigor across the portfolio by identifying emerging risks early, driving mitigations to closure, and providing leadership with a clear view of cross-program threats, dependencies, and decisions.

The Portfolio Risk Program Manager owns the portfolio risk-management operating rhythm. They establish and maintain consistent processes for risk identification, assessment, scoring, ownership, mitigation planning, tracking, and closure across assigned programs. They assess technical maturity, schedule performance, resource constraints, material availability, supplier performance, cost exposure, customer dependencies, security requirements, and contractual considerations to identify risks and opportunities requiring management attention.

The role coordinates routine risk reviews with program managers and functional organizations, including engineering, operations, supply chain, quality, finance, contracts, security, and subcontractors. The Portfolio Risk Program Manager will maintain the integrated portfolio risk and opportunity register; analyze cross-program trends and shared dependencies; assess mitigation effectiveness; and elevate risks requiring Program Manager, customer, or executive intervention. They will ensure risk posture is accurately reflected in program plans, integrated schedules, forecasts, estimate-at-complete updates, proposal assumptions, and management reviews.

In addition to portfolio risk responsibilities, the Portfolio Risk Program Manager will directly manage smaller, discrete programs and special projects. They will maintain execution plans and integrated schedules; track milestones, dependencies, staffing, material status, technical readiness, cost, and deliverables; and lead cross-functional working sessions to drive actions to closure. They will monitor cost and schedule performance, support earned-value inputs and variance explanations as applicable, and develop recovery actions before impacts become critical.

For internal and customer-facing reviews, the Portfolio Risk Program Manager will prepare and coordinate portfolio risk summaries, program status materials, mitigation plans, action logs, decision records, milestone-readiness packages, and follow-up communications. They will support design reviews, program reviews, customer meetings, contract deliverables, production-readiness events, and deliveries by ensuring clear ownership, risk-informed decisions, and closure criteria.

The role will also support proposal activity, follow-on efforts, and contract changes by incorporating current program performance, risk posture, technical maturity, material lead times, staffing needs, and execution lessons learned into proposal schedules, basis-of-estimate inputs, risk registers, and management plans.

The Portfolio Risk Program Manager will have authority to lead risk and execution working sessions, assign and track routine actions, request status from functional organizations, recommend mitigation and recovery actions, and elevate unresolved cross-program risks. The Program Manager retains responsibility for overall portfolio accountability, contractual and baseline decisions, major customer commitments, significant resource conflicts, and executive escalation.

  • Active Top Secret/Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) security clearance.

title: Content Associate, Data
description:
Clarity is redefining how private companies and their shareholders access liquidity. Through its institutional-grade platform, Clarity brings together buyers, sellers, and issuers to facilitate secondary transactions in venture-backed, pre-IPO companies, introducing efficiency, transparency, and standardization to an otherwise opaque asset class.

Recognized as one of Canada's fastest-growing companies and backed by leading U.S. investors, Clarity is profitable, well-capitalized, and building a high-performance team to meet growing demand and pursue new market opportunities.

Interested in learning more about life at Clarity? Check out our careers page to see how you can grow with us!

As a Content Associate, Data at Clarity, you'll help define a new category of investing. Companies are staying private longer and reaching a scale once reserved for the public markets. That changes what a well-balanced investment portfolio looks like, and we want you to build the research that shows investors how. Put simply, you'll help shape a new era in equity investing.

Clarity has transacted more than $6B in private company stock since launching in 2023. Your work will explain how the private markets have performed and how investors can use those insights to shape their portfolios going forward. Using Clarity's proprietary data and third-party research, you'll produce data and write insights for company reports, sector reports, market intelligence, and a monthly newsletter. You'll also own two of these content types from the first data pull to the final published copy, with real autonomy and room to grow as our marketing team scales.

In this role, your responsibilities would include:

  • Owning our Liquidity Thesis series: researching, writing, and updating in-depth reports on the pre-IPO companies investors watch most closely.

  • Turning Clarity's trading data into market intelligence on trading activity, liquidity, market depth, investor participation, and price movement.

  • Building the data and the story behind our annual and quarterly reports on the largest private U.S. companies, including the ones that make the jump to the public markets.

  • Synthesizing third-party research on how institutions, family offices, advisors, and ultra-high-net-worth investors approach private markets.

  • Researching and writing a monthly investor newsletter.

Required Skills:

  • At least four years of experience sourcing, cleaning, and analyzing data, and turning it into clear narratives.

  • Rigorous sourcing habits. You can separate reported facts from company claims and verify statements with a source.

  • Professional experience writing about business, finance, or investing, ideally as a journalist, analyst, researcher, or in-house writer.

  • Examples of published writing on business, financial, or investing topics.

  • The ability to manage several deadlines at once, including weekly company reports, monthly newsletters, and quarterly research.

  • The ability to manipulate data in Excel and data analytics tools such as Omni, Posthog, or others.

  • Working proficiency in AI.

Preferred Skills:

title: Patient Services Representative - Dental
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Patient Service Representative will provide patients and staff with necessary assistance in fulfilling the needs of the center. They are responsible for scheduling dental appointments, patient check in/out, verifying and updating all demographics and insurances, collecting payments, identifying/enrolling patients on the Sliding Fee Scale, processing various forms and documents, and notifying appropriate persons of messages and information as required. Responsible for recording all necessary personal information, securing required signatures, preparing and supplying data to various departments. Provides service internally and externally consistent with ANHC mission, vision and values: Respect, Compassion, Personal Integrity, Excellence & Collaborative Spirit.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Works out of two electronic health record systems (Medical and Dental EHR)
  • Performs opening and closing procedures.
  • Receives all incoming calls in professional manner, answers and accurately processes multi-line phone calls to individual extensions or operator, medical, or billing queues regarding patient billing, appointments, and all general and dental inquiries.
  • Responsible for scheduling, cancelling, or rescheduling dental appointments and maintaining a full schedule for the providers.
  • Makes confirmation calls to all dental appointed patients the day before their appointment after cross referencing both EHR systems and manually updating financials to ensure information in both systems match.
  • Actively checks and address voicemails, emails (work personal/dental shared) and inbound faxes.
  • Receive all (inbound/out bound) fixed and removable dental laboratory cases, updating case status on the log, coordinate laboratory pickup/drop off.
  • Responsible for check in/out processes of each patient. Verifies, updates, and processes various dental/medical forms such as new patient paperwork, demographic updates, dental health histories, sliding fee applications, calculation of income and qualifying patients on the SFS, processing self-declaration applications, health care for the homeless applications. Verifies/updates insurance eligibility and reviews co-pays, co-insurance, deductibles, non-covered charges, and prior authorizations.
  • Collection of appropriate payment based on estimated charge, proper co-pay, deductible, discounted self-pay amount, or past due account balances.
  • Responsible for cash management and daily reconciliation of all financial transactions performed.
  • Limited patient accounts analysis including a general understanding of medical, dental, laboratory, radiology coding and billing standards. This includes CDT, diagnosis, patient rights and responsibilities, third party reimbursement, in/out network, contractual allowances, co-pays and deductibles. Answer and communicate with patients regarding past due balances to help them understand their bill and attempt to collect.
  • Various intermittent, periodic and systematic report completion including unapplied credit, accounts receivable, credit analysis, statement report, billing and communication log, registration and SFS audits.
  • Prepares adjustments for authorization to adjust patient account balances for identified mistakes and bad

debt write-offs.

  • Prepares and processes all dental Release of Information (inbound/outbound) in accordance with the ANHC

policy to patients and other healthcare facilities.

  • Provides patients their treatment plans, reviews their case with the patient and communicates financials and estimated co-pays.
  • Prepares and processes missed appointment letters and mails them to patients and the State of Alaska Department of Health and Social Services when indicated.
  • Cross trained and provides backup for any administrative positions within the department. Responsible for following the medical emergency process, announcing overhead emergency code pages, alerting behavioral health team, medical team in case of a medical emergency, and alerting security guard in urgent/emergency situations and preparing necessary paperwork to first responders.
  • Maintains and fully understands the importance of patient confidentiality and HIPAA compliance.
  • Promotes and provides service excellence to internal and external customers.
  • Work collaboratively with a variety of dental team members including assistants, hygienists, dentists and other ANHC staff such as patient service representatives, providers, nursing staff, case managers/care coordinators, outreach and enrollments, behaviorists, and eligibility personnel to enhance patient experience.
  • Calls in prescribed medication to the pharmacy of patient’s choice if necessary.
  • Effectively communicates with staff and patients.
  • Other duties as assigned.

SUPPORTING DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Monitors reception area and front office for cleanliness and straightens up area as needed.
  • Maintains a clean and orderly work area.
  • Performs translation services if staff member is bilingual.
  • May act as delegated lead or supervisor when the leads or manager are out of the office (during assigned times)
  • Attends required meetings/trainings and participates in committees as requested
  • Assists with training and cross-training

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

ANHC’s Mission, Vision and Values: Actively supports ANHC’s mission, vision and values. Includes using individual skills to add value to the mission: To be a trusted partner in every person’s wellness by providing integrated, compassionate, and high-quality health care, regardless of ability to pay; and vision: Accessible care for a healthy Anchorage. Aligns actions around organizational values of RESPECT, COMPASSION, PERSONAL INTEGRITY, EXCELLENCE and COLLABORATIVE SPIRIT and gives priority to organizational mission, vision and values when making decisions.

Accountability: Takes ownership for delivering on commitments; owns mistakes and uses them as opportunities for learning and development; openly discusses his/her actions and their consequences both good and bad; has an ability to identify strengths and developmental opportunities and leverages insight to make adjustments to improve their effectiveness; courage to have difficult conversations.

Adapting to Change: Accepts and adapts to change in a professionally appropriate and thoughtful manner. Is willing to offer a different perspective or approach and yet knows when and how to stand down graciously and accept a well-thought-out decision. Embraces change.

Confidentiality: Maintains the highest level of confidentiality regarding ANHC records and information relating to ANHC, its customers and employees. Appropriately uses internal confidential information for business purposes only. Responsible for knowledge and compliance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA).

Communicating Effectively: Shares information. Listens and involves others. Clearly conveys ideas in a manner that engages others and helps them understand and retain the message.

Decision Making/Judgment: Approaches problems and decisions methodically and objectively; involves others as needed; uses sound judgment in making decisions and understanding the impact to themselves, customers, their team, and the organization; conducts the appropriate analysis to identify the symptoms and root cause of issues; makes timely decisions.

Delivering High Quality Work: Makes sure responsibilities central to the role meet all requirements and expectations. Finishes tasks promptly and critically reviews work to ensure quality and accuracy. Considers impact of work to others and takes steps to mitigate. Seeks additional work after finishing tasks.

Demonstrating Initiative: Takes action on his/her own without being prompted; handles problems independently; able to resolve issues without relying on extensive help from others; does more than is expected or asked.

Results Orientation: Is focused on outcomes and accomplishments; follows through on commitments; can be counted upon to successfully execute on goals; motivated by achievement and a need for closure; has an attention to detail and is both efficient and effective in achieving a high level of measurable outcomes; persists in achieving goals despite obstacles.

Service Excellence: Has a desire to consistently provide a genuinely exceptional experience to every person, every time. Provides timely and professional service to both internal and external customers; is responsive to customer needs and requests; is always courteous to the customer and considers the needs of the customer when making decisions.

Teamwork: Meets all team deadlines and responsibilities, listens to others and values opinions, helps team and leader to meet goals, welcomes newcomers and promotes a team atmosphere.

PHYSICAL, SENSORY, ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATIONS:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, write, type, grasp, see, hear and speak for long periods of time. Frequent use of computer, keyboard, copy and fax machine and phone. Occasional standing walking, reaching, bending, stooping, lifting and carrying. Lifting, carrying pushing and pulling up to 25 pounds. Must be able to work evening and weekends as scheduled.

Work is performed in a healthcare clinic and office setting. ANHC is a tobacco-free campus.

title: Security FT
description:

Operate Lobby Track system to screen individuals and prevent passage of prohibited visitors into restricted areas. Communicate via radio or telephone to call for assistance from Police, fire, or emergency medical services as the situation dictates. Masten Towers will supply Security polo shirts to each employee. The quantity will be determined by employment status fulltime, part time, or On Call. Masten Towers provides a competitive salary along with a comprehensive benefit package, including medical, dental, vision & life insurance, along with vacation, sick, and holiday pay and a 403(b) retirement plan.


Starting Pay: $16 - $17.00/hour


Essential Functions:

  • Identifying information by categorizing, estimating, recognizing differences or similarities, and detecting changes in circumstances or events.
  • Handling complaints, settling disputes, and resolving grievances and conflicts, or otherwise negotiating with others.
  • Providing information to supervisors, co-workers, and subordinates by telephone, in written form, e-mail, or in person.

title: Customer Message Escalation Assistant
description:
Customer Message Escalation Assistant

Customer Service • Message Escalation

Remote | Full-time | 65,520–68,640 per year

When a routine answer is not enough

Remote customer support often begins with an ordinary question. Occasionally, a customer has already tried the usual steps or needs an answer that the first support team cannot give. The Customer Message Escalation Assistant keeps that transition clear: read the existing conversation, identify what remains unresolved, and send the right context to the colleague responsible for the next decision.

You are not expected to settle account disputes or invent a solution to an unfamiliar problem. The work is careful communication and recordkeeping. A useful escalation tells the receiving team what the customer requested, which information has already been shared, and what answer is still needed. It should also help the customer understand that the issue has been passed on without promising a result or a particular time.

An escalation should describe the question and the checks already made. If a customer says they were promised a different outcome, record the relevant message or reference without deciding who is right. If they report a problem with an online account, describe what they can see and the steps already attempted. Use the priority guidance supplied by the employer and flag uncertainty rather than inventing a deadline. The customer can be told that the matter is under review when that is accurate; the colleague receiving it should see exactly what needs a decision.

What you would actually do

You may receive a message from someone who has contacted support twice, an email that includes several questions, or a case returned by a colleague for one missing detail. Start with the history rather than asking the person to repeat everything. Check the online customer record and any approved guidance. If the information is incomplete, ask a focused question under the employer’s process. If the issue is ready for another team, summarize it in plain language and mark its current status accurately.

After the handoff, keep the case in the correct queue. A request that has been forwarded is not the same as one that has been resolved. If a reply comes back to the original inbox, attach it to the existing case and let the responsible colleague see what changed. Your short status notes make the conversation easier for the next person to continue.

A good escalation also needs the right level of detail. “Customer unhappy” is not enough for the next team to act, while a copy of every earlier sentence can obscure the actual question. State the reason for the handoff and include the relevant reference or prior step. If the customer raises a new issue while the first one is under review, note whether it belongs in the same case under the employer’s procedure. That way, the team can respond to the new concern without losing the original request.

Judgment within clear limits

Some customers want an immediate decision about an exception, a payment, or an account restriction. You can acknowledge the concern and explain the next step using approved wording. You cannot approve a change simply because the person is frustrated. This position rewards someone who listens carefully, records the facts, and knows when to stop guessing.

Clear written customer service is essential. You should be able to organize information from more than one email and use online case tools without mixing customer details. Office administration experience, including shared inboxes or task tracking, can help; direct experience in either area is useful but not required. Applicants with little experience are welcome. The employer can teach its escalation categories and systems, while you bring careful reading and courteous writing.

A suitable home office or similarly private setting can support this remote work. The hiring company will confirm its actual hours, tools, and handling procedures for the opening.

Interested in customer escalations?

Your resume can show how you handled written questions, kept a case organized, or passed an unresolved issue to the right person. Direct escalation experience is welcome, but this introductory role is also open to someone learning the process. Describe the relevant skill through your existing application materials; no separate story is requested.

If you’re selected for the next step, you may be asked to complete an application on the hiring company’s website. The role rewards clear handoffs and sound judgment more than a particular software background.

title: On-Call Field Biologist / Environmental Planner
description:
This Opportunity

At WSP, we are inspired by bringing together the right people to be part of future-focused business objectives that support our diverse client base. Ethical environmental systems and sound project delivery are foundational to shaping a sustainable future. Through environmental consulting, strategic planning, and stakeholder engagement, we help clients understand project impacts and meet regulatory requirements.

Our Planning & Environment group is seeking an On-Call Field Biologist / Environmental Planner based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, or El Paso, Texas. This position will support a diverse range of environmental planning, biological field survey, permitting, and compliance projects across the Desert Southwest.

Your Impact

Design

  • Conduct biological field surveys, habitat assessments, desktop reviews, and environmental data collection under appropriate supervision.
  • Identify plants, wildlife, and sensitive habitats characteristic of the Desert Southwest.
  • Support surveys for special-status species, including endangered plants and avian species.
  • Assist with environmental planning, permitting, impact assessments, construction monitoring, and regulatory compliance.

  • Prepare accurate and defensible survey reports, technical memoranda, field documentation, and supporting materials.
